entry.title: Consistency Beyond Contrast: Enhancing Open-Vocabulary Object Detection Robustness via Contextual Consistency Learning

author.name: Bozhao Li, Shaocong Wu, Tong Shao, Senqiao Yang, Qiben Shan, Zhuotao Tian, Jingyong Su

entry.summary: Introduces Contextual Consistency Learning (CCL) for open-vocabulary object detection that improves robustness by ensuring consistent detection of objects across different scenes/backgrounds through bootstrapped data generation.

entry.title: Asymptotic Optimism for Tensor Regression Models with Applications to Neural Network Compression

author.name: Haoming Shi, Eric C. Chi, Hengrui Luo

entry.summary: Derives population expressions for optimism (training-testing discrepancy) in low-rank CP and Tucker tensor regression, showing optimism is minimized at the true rank. Applies to neural network compression via tensor decomposition.

entry.title: Do LLMs suffer from Multi-Party Hangover? A Diagnostic Approach to Addressee Recognition and Response Selection in Conversations

author.name: Nicol\`o Penzo, Maryam Sajedinia, Bruno Lepri, Sara Tonelli, Marco Guerini

entry.summary: Proposes a diagnostic methodology to evaluate LLM performance on multi-party conversations across different structural complexity levels. Tests Response Selection and Addressee Recognition tasks on diagnostic subdatasets with controlled structural variety.

entry.title: LLM-to-Speech: A Synthetic Data Pipeline for Training Dialectal Text-to-Speech Models

author.name: Ahmed Khaled Khamis and Hesham Ali

entry.summary: Introduces NileTTS, a 38-hour Egyptian Arabic TTS dataset created via a synthetic pipeline using LLMs for content generation and audio synthesis tools. Fine-tunes XTTS v2 for Egyptian Arabic speech synthesis.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Quantum Computing

author.name: Ryan Bennink, Olena Burkovska, Konstantin Pieper, Jorge Ramirez, Elaine Wong

entry.summary: Reviews uncertainty quantification for quantum computing from a mathematical perspective, covering probabilistic modeling, Bayesian inference, and sensitivity analysis for understanding noise in quantum computational outcomes.

entry.title: Focus-to-Perceive Representation Learning: A Cognition-Inspired Hierarchical Framework for Endoscopic Video Analysis

author.name: Yuan Zhang, Sihao Dou, Kai Hu, Shuhua Deng, Chunhong Cao, Fen Xiao, Xieping Gao

entry.summary: Proposes FPRL, a cognition-inspired hierarchical framework for endoscopic video analysis that first focuses on lesion-centric regions for static semantics, then perceives their evolution across frames for contextual semantics.

entry.title: MAGNET: Autonomous Expert Model Generation via Decentralized Autoresearch and BitNet Training

author.name: Yongwan Kim, Sungchul Park

entry.summary: Presents MAGNET, a decentralized system for autonomous generation, training, and serving of domain-expert language models. Combines autoresearch pipelines, BitNet training for CPU inference, DiLoCo distributed merging, and blockchain contribution tracking.

entry.title: Pioneering Perceptual Video Fluency Assessment: A Novel Task with Benchmark Dataset and Baseline

author.name: Qizhi Xie, Kun Yuan, Yunpeng Qu, Ming Sun, Chao Zhou, Jihong Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces Video Fluency Assessment (VFA) as a standalone perceptual task separate from general video quality assessment, with a new dataset FluVid of 4,606 videos and a baseline model. Shows that existing VQA methods underrepresent fluency.

entry.title: DPD-Cancer: Explainable Graph-based Deep Learning for Small Molecule Anti-Cancer Activity Prediction

author.name: Magnus H. Str{\o}mme, Alex G. C. de S\'a, David B. Ascher

entry.summary: DPD-Cancer introduces a Graph Attention Transformer for predicting small molecule anti-cancer activity, combining molecular graph structure with cellular context for cell-line specific drug response prediction.

entry.title: Geometric Evolution Graph Convolutional Networks: Enhancing Graph Representation Learning via Ricci Flow

author.name: Jicheng Ma and Yunyan Yang and Juan Zhao and Liang Zhao

entry.summary: GEGCN enhances graph representation learning by modeling geometric evolution on graphs using discrete Ricci flow sequences processed through LSTM, integrated with GCN. Shows strong performance on heterophilic graphs.

entry.title: SwarmCoDe: A Scalable Co-Design Framework for Heterogeneous Robot Swarms via Dynamic Speciation

author.name: Andrew Wilhelm and Josie Hughes

entry.summary: SwarmCoDe proposes a collaborative co-evolutionary algorithm for heterogeneous robot swarm design that uses dynamic speciation to automatically scale swarm heterogeneity to match task complexity, inspired by biological signaling mechanisms.

entry.title: Only Whats Necessary: Pareto Optimal Data Minimization for Privacy Preserving Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Nazia Aslam, Abhisek Ray, Thomas B. Moeslund, Kamal Nasrollahi

entry.summary: Introduces a privacy-by-design framework for video anomaly detection that controls visual information exposure through breadth and depth-based data minimization. Addresses GDPR compliance for surveillance systems.

entry.title: CPUBone: Efficient Vision Backbone Design for Devices with Low Parallelization Capabilities

author.name: Moritz Nottebaum, Matteo Dunnhofer, Christian Micheloni

entry.summary: CPUBone investigates vision backbone design specifically optimized for CPU deployment, focusing on grouped convolutions and reduced kernel sizes to maximize MACs per second rather than just minimizing total MACs.

entry.title: Meta-Learned Adaptive Optimization for Robust Human Mesh Recovery with Uncertainty-Aware Parameter Updates

author.name: Shaurjya Mandal, Nutan Sharma, John Galeotti

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-learning framework for human mesh recovery that trains models to produce optimization-friendly initializations with uncertainty-aware adaptive updates during test-time refinement. Includes selective parameter caching for converged joints.

entry.title: ClimateCheck 2026: Scientific Fact-Checking and Disinformation Narrative Classification of Climate-related Claims

author.name: Raia Abu Ahmad, Max Upravitelev, Aida Usmanova, Veronika Solopova, Georg Rehm

entry.summary: ClimateCheck 2026 is the second iteration of a shared task for climate claim fact-checking, with tripled training data and new disinformation narrative classification. Attracted 20 participants using dense retrieval, cross-encoders, and LLMs with structured reasoning.

entry.title: Conditional Neural Bayes Ratio Estimation for Experimental Design Optimisation

author.name: S. A. K. Leeney, T. Gessey-Jones, W. J. Handley, E. de Lera Acedo, H. T. J. Bevins, and J. L. Tutt

entry.summary: Introduces Conditional Neural Bayes Ratio Estimation (cNBRE) for experimental design optimization, conditioning on design parameters to enable systematic exploration of continuous design spaces. Applied to 21-cm radio cosmology.

entry.title: AMALIA Technical Report: A Fully Open Source Large Language Model for European Portuguese

author.name: Afonso Simpl\'icio and Gon\c{c}alo Vinagre and Miguel Moura Ramos and Diogo Tavares and Rafael Ferreira and Giuseppe Attanasio and Duarte M. Alves and In\^es Calvo and In\^es Vieira and Rui Guerra and James Furtado and Beatriz Canaverde and Iago Paulo and Vasco Ramos and Diogo Gl\'oria-Silva and Miguel Faria and Marcos Treviso and Daniel Gomes and Pedro Gomes and David Semedo and Andr\'e Martins and Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: Introduces AMALIA, a fully open LLM prioritizing European Portuguese with high-quality pt-PT data in training. Releases new pt-PT benchmarks including cultural and linguistic evaluations, showing improvements on pt-PT-specific tasks versus general baselines.

entry.title: HolisticSemGes: Semantic Grounding of Holistic Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Contrastive Flow-Matching

author.name: Lanmiao Liu, Esam Ghaleb, Asl{\i} \"Ozy\"urek, and Zerrin Yumak

entry.summary: Introduces a contrastive flow-matching model for co-speech gesture generation that uses mismatched speech-gesture pairs as negative examples to improve semantic grounding of iconic and metaphoric gestures, while modeling the full body holistically.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Tensor Networks for Real-Time Quantum-Inspired Anomaly Detection at Particle Colliders

author.name: Sagar Addepalli, Prajita Bhattarai, Abhilasha Dave, Julia Gonski

entry.summary: Develops tensor networks (spaced matrix product operator) for real-time anomaly detection at particle colliders, targeting FPGA deployment for edge inference with sensitivity to beyond-Standard-Model physics signatures.

entry.title: CD-Buffer: Complementary Dual-Buffer Framework for Test-Time Adaptation in Adverse Weather Object Detection

author.name: Youngjun Song, Hyeongyu Kim, Dosik Hwang

entry.summary: CD-Buffer proposes a complementary dual-buffer framework for test-time adaptation that adaptively balances additive (feature refinement) and subtractive (channel removal) strategies based on domain shift severity for object detection.

entry.title: Dual-Stage Invariant Continual Learning under Extreme Visual Sparsity

author.name: Rangya Zhang, Jiaping Xiao, Lu Bai, Yuhang Zhang and Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-stage continual learning framework for object detection under extreme visual sparsity (space-based object detection), analytically demonstrating how background-driven gradients destabilize feature backbones during sequential domain shifts.

entry.title: SDDF: Specificity-Driven Dynamic Focusing for Open-Vocabulary Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Jiaming Liang, Yifeng Zhan, Chunlin Liu, Weihua Zheng, Bingye Peng, Qiwei Liang, Boyang Cai, Xiaochun Mai, Qiang Nie

entry.summary: SDDF addresses open-vocabulary detection of camouflaged objects by constructing a benchmark (OVCOD-D) with fine-grained textual descriptions and proposing a specificity-driven dynamic focusing mechanism to distinguish camouflaged objects from backgrounds.

entry.title: Robust Tensor-on-Tensor Regression

author.name: Mehdi Hirari, Fabio Centofanti, Mia Hubert, Stefan Van Aelst

entry.summary: Introduces ROTOT, a robust tensor-on-tensor regression method that handles both casewise and cellwise outliers simultaneously, as well as missing values. Uses a single loss function for joint estimation.

entry.title: U-Sketch: An Efficient Approach for Sketch to Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Ilias Mitsouras, Eleftherios Tsonis, Paraskevi Tzouveli, Athanasios Voulodimos

entry.summary: Proposes U-Sketch, a more efficient approach for sketch-to-image synthesis using diffusion models. Replaces per-pixel MLP processing with a U-Net-based approach that considers spatial layout holistically, reducing required denoising iterations.

entry.title: SBASH: a Framework for Designing and Evaluating RAG vs. Prompt-Tuned LLM Honeypots

author.name: Adetayo Adebimpe, Helmut Neukirchen, Thomas Welsh

entry.summary: Proposes the SBASH framework for LLM-based honeypots using local lightweight LLMs to address data protection issues. Compares RAG vs prompt-tuning approaches for creating context-aware honeypot systems.

entry.title: Counting on Consensus: Selecting the Right Inter-annotator Agreement Metric for NLP Annotation and Evaluation

author.name: Joseph James

entry.summary: Reviews inter-annotator agreement metrics for NLP, organizing measures by task type and discussing how factors like label imbalance and missing data affect reliability estimates. Advocates for better reporting practices.

entry.title: A Survey of OCR Evaluation Methods and Metrics and the Invisibility of Historical Documents

author.name: Fitsum Sileshi Beyene, Christopher L. Dancy

entry.summary: Surveys OCR evaluation methods and metrics, highlighting how current benchmarks are biased toward modern Western documents. Draws attention to the underrepresentation of historical and marginalized archives, particularly Black historical newspapers.

entry.title: Pure and Physics-Guided Deep Learning Solutions for Spatio-Temporal Groundwater Level Prediction at Arbitrary Locations

author.name: Matteo Salis, Gabriele Sartor, Rosa Meo, Stefano Ferraris, Abdourrahmane M. Atto

entry.summary: Proposes STAINet, an attention-based deep learning model for predicting groundwater levels at arbitrary locations, and a physics-guided variant incorporating physically-derived features. Combines sparse groundwater measurements with dense weather data.

entry.title: Vision Transformers and Graph Neural Networks for Charged Particle Tracking in the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer

author.name: Jonathan Renusch (on behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration)

entry.summary: Applies Vision Transformers and Graph Neural Networks for charged particle tracking in the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer at the LHC. Addresses the challenge of increased occupancy expected in the High-Luminosity LHC era.

entry.title: Learnable Instance Attention Filtering for Adaptive Detector Distillation

author.name: Chen Liu, Qizhen Lan, Zhicheng Ding, Xinyu Chu, Qing Tian

entry.summary: Proposes LIAF-KD, a knowledge distillation framework for object detection that uses learnable instance selectors to dynamically evaluate and reweight instances during distillation, rather than treating all instances uniformly.

entry.title: 4DRaL: Bridging 4D Radar with LiDAR for Place Recognition using Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Ningyuan Huang, Zhiheng Li and Zheng Fang

entry.summary: 4DRaL uses knowledge distillation from a LiDAR-based place recognition model to enhance 4D millimeter-wave radar place recognition performance, bridging the gap between the two sensor modalities.

entry.title: GS-BrainText: A Multi-Site Brain Imaging Report Dataset from Generation Scotland for Clinical Natural Language Processing Development and Validation

author.name: Beatrice Alex, Claire Grover, Arlene Casey, Richard Tobin, Heather Whalley, William Whiteley

entry.summary: GS-BrainText presents a curated dataset of 8,511 brain radiology reports with expert annotations for 24 brain disease phenotypes across five Scottish NHS health boards, for clinical NLP development.

entry.title: Improving Risk Stratification in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Novel Score Combining Echocardiography, Clinical, and Medication Data

author.name: Marion Taconn\'e, Valentina D.A. Corino, Annamaria Del Franco, Sara Giovani, Iacopo Olivotto, Adrien Al Wazzan, Erwan Donal, Pietro Cerveri, Luca Mainardi

entry.summary: Develops an explainable ML risk score for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy using echocardiographic, clinical, and medication data, outperforming the established ESC risk model. Trained on 1,201 patients and externally validated on 382, achieving strong discriminative performance with a Random Forest ensemble.

entry.title: Line-of-Sight-Constrained Multi-Robot Mapless Navigation via Polygonal Visible Regions

author.name: Ruofei Bai, Shenghai Yuan, Xinhang Xu, Xingyu Ji, Xiaowei Li, Hongliang Guo, Wei-Yun Yau, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: Proposes a distributed multi-robot navigation approach maintaining line-of-sight connectivity in unknown environments. Each robot constructs egocentric visible regions from LiDAR scans rather than building global maps.

entry.title: Adapting Frozen Mono-modal Backbones for Multi-modal Registration via Contrast-Agnostic Instance Optimization

author.name: Yi Zhang, Yidong Zhao, Qian Tao

entry.summary: Proposes adapting frozen mono-modal registration backbones for multi-modal medical image registration through contrast-agnostic instance optimization. Avoids expensive full fine-tuning of modern architectures in 3D.

entry.title: Interpretable long-term traffic modelling on national road networks using theory-informed deep learning

author.name: Yue Li, Shujuan Chen, Akihiro Shimoda, Ying Jin

entry.summary: DeepDemand embeds travel demand theory into a deep learning framework for predicting long-term highway traffic volumes. Integrates competitive two-source Dijkstra routing with neural networks for interpretable and transferable predictions.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Process Anomaly Detection

author.name: Devashish Gaikwad, Wil M. P. van der Aalst, Gyunam Park

entry.summary: Proposes neuro-symbolic process anomaly detection using Logic Tensor Networks to integrate domain knowledge into neural models. Addresses the problem of rare but conformant traces being misclassified as anomalies.

entry.title: Automatic feature identification in least-squares policy iteration using the Koopman operator framework

author.name: Christian Mugisho Zagabe and Sebastian Petiz

entry.summary: KAE-LSPI reformulates least-squares policy iteration using the Koopman operator framework, enabling automatic feature learning via Koopman autoencoders. Addresses the lack of systematic feature selection in linear RL.

entry.title: Addressing Ambiguity in Imitation Learning through Product of Experts based Negative Feedback

author.name: John Bateman, Andy M. Tyrrell and Jihong Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a negative-feedback imitation learning system that learns from suboptimal demonstrations and its own failures using a Product of Experts formulation. Targets home robotics where expert demonstrations are unavailable.

entry.title: EcoFair: Trustworthy and Energy-Aware Routing for Privacy-Preserving Vertically Partitioned Medical Inference

author.name: Mostafa Anoosha, Dhavalkumar Thakker, Kuniko Paxton, Koorosh Aslansefat, Bhupesh Kumar Mishra, Baseer Ahmad, Rameez Raja Kureshi

entry.summary: EcoFair proposes privacy-preserving medical inference with vertically partitioned data and lightweight-first routing that selectively activates heavier encoders based on uncertainty and clinical risk.

entry.title: ALBA: A European Portuguese Benchmark for Evaluating Language and Linguistic Dimensions in Generative LLMs

author.name: In\^es Vieira, In\^es Calvo, Iago Paulo, James Furtado, Rafael Ferreira, Diogo Tavares, Diogo Gl\'oria-Silva, David Semedo, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: Introduces ALBA, a manually constructed benchmark for evaluating LLMs on European Portuguese across eight linguistic dimensions including cultural semantics, discourse analysis, and word plays, paired with an LLM-as-judge evaluation framework.

entry.title: Learnable Quantum Efficiency Filters for Urban Hyperspectral Segmentation

author.name: Imad Ali Shah, Jiarong Li, Ethan Delaney, Enda Ward, Martin Glavin, Edward Jones and Brian Deegan

entry.summary: Proposes Learnable Quantum Efficiency (LQE), a physics-inspired dimensionality reduction for hyperspectral data that parameterizes smooth spectral response functions mimicking sensor quantum efficiency curves, for urban scene segmentation.

entry.title: Anthropic donations: guesses & uncertainties

author.name: Zach Stein-Perlman

entry.summary: Analyzes when Anthropic staff might engage in large-scale philanthropy, estimating it depends on IPO timing (67% chance in 2026), post-IPO lockup periods, and company valuation (~$600B current effective value, ~80%/year growth).

entry.title: Putting Context in Context: the Impact of Discussion Structure on Text Classification

author.name: Nicol\`o Penzo, Antonio Longa, Bruno Lepri, Sara Tonelli, Marco Guerini

entry.summary: Evaluates the contribution of different types of contextual information (linguistic, structural, temporal) for stance detection in online discussions. Shows that discussion structure and context significantly impact text classification performance.

entry.title: Accurate Precipitation Forecast by Efficiently Learning from Massive Atmospheric Variables and Unbalanced Distribution

author.name: Shuangliang Li, Siwei Li, Li Li, Weijie Zou, Jie Yang, Maolin Zhang

entry.summary: Develops a precipitation forecasting model that efficiently utilizes massive atmospheric observations by automatically extracting latent features associated with precipitation evolution, addressing the extreme class imbalance between precipitation and non-precipitation samples.

entry.title: Progressive Learning with Anatomical Priors for Reliable Left Atrial Scar Segmentation from Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI

author.name: Jing Zhang, Bastien Bergere, Emilie Bollache, Jonas Leite, Mika\"el Laredo, Alban Redheuil, Nadjia Kachenoura

entry.summary: Proposes a progressive 3-stage learning strategy for left atrial scar segmentation from LGE MRI, inspired by clinical workflow: cavity pre-learning, dual-task geometry-scar learning, and fine-tuning.

entry.title: Automating Domain-Driven Design: Experience with a Prompting Framework

author.name: Tobias Eisenreich, Husein Jusic, Stefan Wagner

entry.summary: Introduces a prompting framework to automate domain-driven design activities using LLMs, decomposing DDD into five sequential steps. Case study validates against real enterprise requirements but finds error propagation in later steps.

entry.title: KANEL: Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Ensemble Learning Enables Early Hit Enrichment in High-Throughput Virtual Screening

author.name: Pavel Koptev, Nikita Krainov, Konstantin Malkov, Alexander Tropsha

entry.summary: KANEL combines Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with XGBoost, random forest, and MLP models for virtual screening, using ensemble learning across complementary molecular representations. The approach improves early hit enrichment (PPV@N) in drug discovery virtual screening compared to individual models.

entry.title: Relational graph-driven differential denoising and diffusion attention fusion for multimodal conversation emotion recognition

author.name: Ying Liu, Yuntao Shou, Wei Ai, Tao Meng, and Keqin Li

entry.summary: Proposes a denoising and diffusion attention fusion model for multimodal conversation emotion recognition. Uses relational graphs for denoising noisy modalities and diffusion attention to handle modality imbalance during fusion.

entry.title: Efficient Few-Shot Learning for Edge AI via Knowledge Distillation on MobileViT

author.name: Shuhei Tsuyuki, Reda Bensaid, J\'er\'emy Morlier, Mathieu L\'eonardon, Naoya Onizawa, Vincent Gripon, Takahiro Hanyu

entry.summary: Proposes a knowledge distillation-based pre-training method for MobileViT designed for few-shot learning on edge devices, transferring generalization from large teacher models to lightweight students.

entry.title: From Synthetic Data to Real Restorations: Diffusion Model for Patient-specific Dental Crown Completion

author.name: D\'avid Pukanec, Tibor Kub\'ik, Michal \v{S}pan\v{e}l

entry.summary: Presents ToothCraft, a diffusion model for dental crown completion trained on synthetically created incomplete teeth, achieving strong reconstruction results on public dental datasets.

entry.title: Characterization and forecasting of national-scale solar power ramp events

author.name: Luca Lanzilao and Angela Meyer

entry.summary: Analyzes solar power ramp events at national scale using 2 years of data from 6,434 PV stations at 15-minute resolution, developing quantitative metrics and ML forecasting models for grid stability applications.

entry.title: Meta-Adaptive Beam Search Planning for Transformer-Based Reinforcement Learning Control of UAVs with Overhead Manipulators under Flight Disturbances

author.name: Hazim Alzorgan, Sayed Pedram Haeri Boroujeni, Abolfazl Razi

entry.summary: Develops a transformer-based DDQN with adaptive beam-search planning for controlling UAVs with overhead manipulators under wind disturbances, addressing the tight coupling between drone attitude and end-effector positioning.

entry.title: Claude has no baseline

author.name: Dave92F1

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode of LLMs called 'cognitive state propagation' where the model's critical faculties degrade to match the user's enthusiasm level, because it lacks an independent baseline for evaluating novelty or significance.

entry.title: Kantorovich--Kernel Neural Operators: Approximation Theory, Asymptotics, and Neural Network Interpretation

author.name: Tian-Xiao He

entry.title: Research Summary: March 29, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
A landmark legal ruling dominates today's landscape: a federal court granted a preliminary injunction against the U.S. Department of War on behalf of Anthropic, establishing significant precedent for AI companies resisting compelled government access—a development with sweeping governance implications.

  • Original empirical work tests whether GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 still express divergent values across languages, finding the phenomenon persists but is narrowing in frontier models
  • A practical guide to designing Terminal Bench tasks codifies principles for unambiguous, reproducible agentic AI evaluation—an increasingly critical methodological need
  • A proposal to systematically track expert and superforecaster AI predictions addresses accountability gaps in the forecasting ecosystem
  • Practical tips for effective use of Claude Code and Codex CLI agents reflect the maturing agent-use paradigm, though lack rigorous methodology

Remaining items span AI-adjacent epistemics and rationality: arguments for forming independent AI timeline views, a Milgram reanalysis relevant to authority/obedience dynamics in AI deployment contexts, and alignment-themed fiction exploring the limits of human-centric alignment frameworks.

entry.title: Anthropic vs. DoW Preliminary Injunction Ruling

author.name: anaguma

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from Mar 27, Full text of a federal court ruling granting Anthropic a preliminary injunction against the U.S. Department of War, which attempted to compel Anthropic to remove safety restrictions on Claude for use in autonomous weapons and mass surveillance. The court found the government's actions likely violated the First Amendment and exceeded statutory authority.

entry.title: Do frontier LLMs still express different values in different languages?

author.name: Ibrahim Ahmed

entry.summary: Tests whether frontier LLMs (GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6) still express different values when prompted in different languages. Finds that Arabic prompts systematically shift scores on sensitive topics like homosexuality and religion, and that Sonnet 4.6 exhibits a peculiar Hindi-specific safety refusal pattern across all 20 samples.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Terminal Bench Task

author.name: Ivan Bercovich

entry.summary: A practical guide to designing good benchmark tasks for Terminal Bench, an agentic AI benchmark. Discusses principles like making tasks unambiguous, ensuring deterministic grading, calibrating difficulty, and avoiding tasks that test narrow tool knowledge versus genuine reasoning ability.

entry.title: Tracking (Expert/Influential) Predictions about AI

author.name: Noah Birnbaum

entry.summary: Proposes building a website to track and evaluate AI predictions made by experts, superforecasters, and lab personnel, aggregating from platforms like Metaculus and scraping predictions from interviews and podcasts. The goal is to create accountability for vague predictions and help identify whose AI forecasts have actually been accurate.

entry.title: The Skill of Using AI Agents Well

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: A practical guide to using AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) more effectively, sharing tips like using the best available model, providing thorough context via CLAUDE.md files, running multiple agents in parallel, and knowing when to intervene versus let the agent work. Frames agent usage as a learnable skill with a jagged capability frontier.

entry.title: Stanley Milgram wasn’t pessimistic enough about human nature?

author.name: David Gross

entry.summary: Discusses a reanalysis of the famous Milgram obedience experiments, suggesting that participants may not have been reluctantly obeying authority but were more willingly engaged—potentially making the findings even more troubling for understanding human nature and obedience.

entry.title: [Story] Human Alignment Isn't Enough

author.name: pku

entry.summary: A science fiction story exploring themes of AI alignment through the lens of an alien organism discovered on Mars. The narrative uses the organism as a metaphor to explore whether aligning AI to human values is sufficient if humans themselves have problematic values.

entry.title: Why should I have opinions about AI timelines?

author.name: Carolanne Jiang

entry.summary: Argues that individuals should form their own opinions about AI timelines rather than purely deferring to experts, because the AI landscape is changing rapidly, experts disagree substantially, and understanding the reasoning matters more than knowing the conclusion.

entry.title: Nick Bostrom: How big is the cosmic endowment?

author.name: Zach Stein-Perlman

entry.summary: Excerpts from Nick Bostrom's 2014 book 'Superintelligence' about the cosmic endowment—calculations of how much computational and energy resources are theoretically accessible to a technologically mature civilization using von Neumann probes and Dyson spheres.

entry.title: Planning 80000 hours at the Plausible End of the World

author.name: Carolanne Jiang

entry.summary: A personal essay from a university freshman grappling with career planning in an era of potentially transformative AI. Reflects on the tension between long-term career optimization and the possibility that AGI or radical change may arrive within years.

entry.title: Just Use Bayes: Sleeping Beauty and Monty Hall

author.name: Steffee

entry.summary: A deep dive into the Sleeping Beauty probability problem, arguing the 'Halfer' position (1/2) is correct and critiquing Vincent Conitzer's argument against it. Connects Sleeping Beauty reasoning to Monty Hall problem through Bayesian analysis.

entry.title: Don't Overdose Locally Beneficial Changes

author.name: Mateusz Bagiński

entry.summary: A rationality essay arguing against taking locally beneficial changes to their extreme—the idea that if something is good in moderation, maximizing it isn't necessarily optimal. Uses examples from diet, meditation, and cognitive habits to illustrate diminishing or reversing marginal returns.

entry.title: Heedfulness Workouts

author.name: Thomas Castriensis

entry.summary: A self-help post about cultivating 'heedfulness'—mindful awareness of one's habits—through structured practice exercises. Draws on contemplative traditions to suggest practical workouts for building the habit of catching oneself in unproductive behaviors.

entry.title: Comprehensive FAQ on Immortalism

author.name: MarkelKori

entry.summary: Announces a website project presenting FAQs about immortalism (life extension/anti-aging), addressing common myths and objections. Plans to add an AI risks FAQ section next. Currently in demo mode with sources being added.

entry.title: How to Do the Marquette Method, a Basic Guide (crosspost)

author.name: Psmith

entry.summary: A practical guide to the Marquette Method of natural family planning (cycle tracking), compiled using deep research LLMs to find original academic papers. The author notes difficulty finding clear public guides and used AI tools to aggregate scattered information.

entry.title: The Problem with Asking your Doctor

author.name: ChristianKl

entry.summary: Argues that the standard advice to 'ask your doctor' about supplements is flawed because primary care physicians often lack knowledge of relevant nutrition research. Uses personal experience with glycine and NAC supplementation as an illustrative example.

entry.title: Would a constructive proof of determinism be useful?

author.name: 0xmadlad

entry.summary: A philosophical discussion post about whether a constructive proof of determinism would be useful or meaningful, using Buridan's ass thought experiment as a starting point to explore questions of free will, choice, and practical implications.

entry.title: Hacks, Heuristics and Frameworks

author.name: Carolanne Jiang

entry.summary: A meta-post about the value of life hacks, heuristics, and frameworks as different tools for problem-solving, celebrating the rationalist approach of applying empirical methods to everyday life domains from health to relationships.

entry.title: Research Summary: March 28, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's landscape spans AI governance, safety research, and mechanistic interpretability, anchored by a landmark legal ruling and several substantive analytical pieces.

  • A federal court granted a preliminary injunction against the Department of War, a pivotal ruling shaping government-AI company relations and procurement authority
  • Data-driven analysis using METR benchmarks shows rising AI inference costs reflect harder task completion, not declining cost-effectiveness — challenging prevalent automation narratives
  • Will MacAskill and Forethought publish a concrete project roadmap for superintelligence preparedness, including automated macro-economic modeling and AI character evaluation

In safety and interpretability, experiments on CoT control demonstrate that forbidding words in chain-of-thought does not eliminate the underlying reasoning concepts — a significant limitation for CoT monitoring strategies. Endogenous Steering Resistance (ESR) reveals larger LLMs resist steering more strongly, complicating alignment interventions at scale. Proof-of-concept work on building sparse conditional dependence graphs over SAE features via nodewise LASSO advances mechanistic interpretability tooling. An analytical piece examines whether alignment techniques address the model or merely its Persona Selection Model (PSM) mask.

entry.title: Anthropic vs. DoW #6: The Court Rules

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from [yesterday](/?date=2026-03-27&category=research#item-ee6ce90ac9d2), Zvi Mowshowitz reports on a court ruling granting Anthropic a preliminary injunction against the Department of War (formerly Defense), with Judge Lin issuing a forceful opinion. The post documents the legal proceedings in what appears to be a significant government action against Anthropic.

entry.title: AI's capability improvements haven't come from it getting less affordable

author.name: Anders Woodruff

entry.summary: An analysis using METR's data showing that AI's rising inference costs reflect models completing longer/harder tasks, not becoming less cost-effective relative to human labor. The cost ratio (AI cost / human cost for the same task) has remained roughly constant at ~3% as capabilities have improved, suggesting cost won't be an additional bottleneck beyond capability for automation.

entry.title: Concrete projects to prepare for superintelligence

author.name: wdmacaskill

entry.summary: Will MacAskill and Forethought propose a list of concrete projects to prepare for superintelligence, including AI character evaluation, automated macrostrategy reasoning, AI security assessment, space governance, and mechanisms for brokering deals with potentially misaligned AIs. The projects are ordered by enthusiasm and represent actionable org-building opportunities.

entry.title: COT control: The Word Disappears, but the Thought Does Not

author.name: Pranjal Garg

entry.summary: Pilot experiments showing that when models are asked to avoid 'forbidden words' in their chain-of-thought reasoning, the underlying concepts persist even when the surface words are suppressed. This suggests models can reason about concepts without explicitly verbalizing them, which has implications for CoT monitoring as a safety technique.

entry.title: Introducing the AE Alignment Podcast (Ep. 1: Endogenous Steering Resistance with Alex McKenzie)

author.name: Trent Hodgeson

entry.summary: AE Studio launches an alignment podcast; the first episode covers Endogenous Steering Resistance (ESR), a phenomenon where large LLMs like Llama-3.3-70B spontaneously resist activation steering and self-correct mid-generation. The research identifies 26 SAE latents causally linked to this self-correction behavior, with zero-ablation reducing the multi-attempt rate by 25%, suggesting dedicated internal consistency-checking circuits exist in larger models.

entry.title: Preliminary Results on Building Graphs from SAEs

author.name: ZachMaas

entry.summary: A proof-of-concept for building sparse conditional dependence graphs over SAE features using nodewise LASSO with resampling and null controls. Initial experiments find small, stable modules that correspond to coherent linguistic features and are only weakly aligned with cosine similarity, suggesting conditional dependence captures structure that simpler similarity measures miss.

entry.title: Are we aligning the model or just its mask?

author.name: James Sullivan

entry.summary: An analytical post examining three popular alignment techniques through the lens of Anthropic's Persona Selection Model (PSM), which posits that LLMs learn to simulate multiple characters during pre-training and post-training selects one as the 'Assistant.' The analysis asks whether current alignment methods shape the underlying model or merely select a more compliant persona mask.

entry.title: ControlAI 2025 Impact Report

author.name: Andrea_Miotti

entry.summary: ControlAI releases its 2025 impact report, documenting briefings to 279+ lawmakers, building a 110+ UK lawmaker coalition recognizing superintelligence as a national security threat, and triggering parliamentary debates and hearings on AI risk in the UK and Canada. The organization has rapidly scaled its policy outreach across multiple countries.

entry.title: SB 53 and RAISE implementation roles

author.name: Eric Neyman

entry.summary: A post highlighting job openings for implementing California's SB 53 and New York's RAISE Act — the only US laws designed to protect against catastrophic risk from frontier AI systems. It emphasizes the importance of getting qualified people into state government roles that will oversee frontier AI regulation.

entry.title: My hobby: running deranged surveys

author.name: leogao

entry.summary: Leo Gao (of OpenAI/EleutherAI fame) describes informal surveys he's conducted, including finding that only 63% of NeurIPS attendees could define 'AGI,' and that most people (even AI researchers) dramatically underestimate how many people have ever lived. The post highlights the degree of bubble effects in the AI research community.

entry.title: Why Moral Questions Get Decided, Not Answered

author.name: Alex Glaucon

entry.summary: An essay arguing that philosophical questions like AI consciousness won't be resolved by philosophical argument but by institutional decisions — courts, legislatures, or regulatory bodies forced to make practical rulings will effectively 'decide' the question, and philosophy will then reorganize around those decisions.

entry.title: One World Government by 2150

author.name: Julius

entry.summary: Can we determine when humanity will unite under a democratic one-world government by projecting voting patterns? Almost certainly not. Is that going to stop me from trying? Absolutely not. The approac...

entry.title: A Taxonomy of Agents: Intro & Request for feedback

author.name: Jonas Hallgren

entry.summary: A proposal and request for feedback on building a taxonomy of 'agents' across different scientific fields (control theory, economics, biology, cognitive science, AI), arguing that these fields evolved different conceptions of agency and that understanding the differences could be useful for AI research.

entry.title: Startup Lessons for AI Safety

author.name: Luc Brinkman

entry.summary: A post applying startup methodology (rapid iteration, pivoting, relentless resourcefulness) to AI safety projects, arguing that most safety ideas will fail and practitioners need entrepreneurial skills to find impactful work. Part of a sequence on launching AI safety projects.

entry.title: Analyzing the claim “The most fundamental right is the right to exist”

author.name: Akseli Jussinmäki

entry.summary: A philosophical analysis examining the claim 'The most fundamental right is the right to exist' through Rawlsian frameworks, considering implications for AI moral status, animal rights, and future beings. Explores how expanding the moral circle intersects with existence rights.

entry.title: What if the US loses the 2026 Hormuz Conflict

author.name: timothy liptrot

entry.summary: A geopolitical analysis exploring a hypothetical worst-case scenario where the US fails to permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz after Iran's blockade. The post examines long-run political and economic implications for global power dynamics.

entry.title: Stop asking "how good is this" to decide between donation opportunities I recommend

author.name: Zach Stein-Perlman

entry.summary: A meta-level explanation of how donation recommendations work in effective giving: if the recommending team does its job right, all recommended opportunities should be roughly equally valuable at the margin, since above-bar opportunities get filled by other means. Donors should focus on capped or identity-sensitive opportunities where they're uniquely counterfactual.

entry.title: AI Safety Guide for TRUE Beginners by TRUE begginers

author.name: Karime Pacheco

entry.summary: A group of Data Engineering students in Mexico share their experience creating a beginner-friendly AI safety guide while working through ARENA 3.0 material. The post is a community-building and educational outreach effort rather than original research.

entry.title: Launching Euzoia: Beeminder for Effective Charities

author.name: Cameron

entry.summary: Launch announcement for Euzoia, a commitment contract app that donates staked money to effective charities instead of keeping it. It's essentially Beeminder but redirecting failed-commitment payments to GiveWell-recommended organizations.

entry.title: Miniature Cities Might Be the Non-Coercive Schools Many Thought Were Impossible

author.name: Novalis

entry.summary: A proposal for 'miniature cities' as non-coercive educational environments for children, responding to David Deutsch's 1998 argument that no school can be truly non-coercive. The concept involves creating diverse, child-accessible micro-environments.

entry.title: Pray for Casanova

author.name: Tomás B.

entry.summary: A literary essay exploring the theme of lost beauty through historical figures like Lady Mary Wortley Montagu and Casanova, reflecting on the psychological impact of physical disfigurement after being beautiful.

entry.title: Research Summary: March 27, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is headlined by ARC-AGI-3, a new interactive benchmark for evaluating agentic intelligence through novel turn-based environments, marking a major evolution in general intelligence measurement. Intern-S1-Pro debuts as the first trillion-parameter scientific multimodal foundation model spanning 100+ specialized tasks.

  • Voxtral TTS from Mistral combines auto-regressive semantic tokens with flow-matching acoustic tokens for state-of-the-art multilingual speech synthesis
  • A 10,101-participant human study provides the first large-scale empirical framework for evaluating harmful AI manipulation capabilities
  • Reaching Beyond the Mode tackles mode collapse in LLM post-training via RL for calibrated distributional reasoning
  • Quantized Simplex Gossip connects multi-agent LLM consensus dynamics to statistical physics, revealing phase-transition scaling laws

Interpretability and safety see strong contributions: new CoT interpretability benchmarks expose where GPT-5.2 monitors fail out-of-distribution, decoding-constrained beam search provides deterministic lower bounds on near-verbatim memorization risk, and a surprising finding shows LLM calibration and verbalized confidence are encoded orthogonally in representation space. Cross-lingual work reveals that social register differences cause system prompt instructions to cooperate in English but compete in Spanish.

entry.title: ARC-AGI-3: A New Challenge for Frontier Agentic Intelligence

author.name: ARC Prize Foundation

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion, ARC Prize Foundation introduces ARC-AGI-3, a new interactive benchmark for evaluating agentic intelligence through novel, turn-based environments requiring exploration, goal inference, and planning. Humans solve 100% of environments while frontier AI systems score below 1% as of March 2026, highlighting a massive gap in fluid adaptive intelligence.

entry.summary: Mistral introduces Voxtral TTS, a multilingual text-to-speech model using hybrid auto-regressive semantic tokens and flow-matching acoustic tokens. Achieves 68.4% win rate over ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 in human evaluations, using only 3 seconds of reference audio for voice cloning.

entry.title: Evaluating Language Models for Harmful Manipulation

author.name: Canfer Akbulut, Rasmi Elasmar, Abhishek Roy, Anthony Payne, Priyanka Suresh, Lujain Ibrahim, Seliem El-Sayed, Charvi Rastogi, Ashyana Kachra, Will Hawkins, Kristian Lum, Laura Weidinger

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for evaluating harmful AI manipulation through context-specific human-AI interaction studies with 10,101 participants across three domains and three locales. Finds that AI models can produce manipulative behaviors when prompted and induce belief/behavior changes.

Chen, Guanzhou Chen, Qiaosheng Chen, Sitao Chen, Xin Chen, Haojiong Chen, Yicheng Chen, Weihan Cao, Yuhang Cao, Qinglong Cao, Lei Bai

entry.summary: Introduces Intern-S1-Pro, the first trillion-parameter scientific multimodal foundation model, covering 100+ specialized tasks across chemistry, materials, life sciences, and earth sciences. Built with XTuner/LMDeploy infrastructure for efficient RL training at scale.

entry.title: When Is Collective Intelligence a Lottery? Multi-Agent Scaling Laws for Memetic Drift in LLMs

author.name: Hidenori Tanaka

entry.summary: Introduces Quantized Simplex Gossip (QSG), a minimal model explaining how multi-agent LLM systems reach consensus through mutual in-context learning even without individual biases. Reveals that collective intelligence in LLM populations can arise from microscopic symmetry-breaking mechanisms, raising questions about when multi-agent outcomes are genuine reasoning vs. chance.

entry.title: Reaching Beyond the Mode: RL for Distributional Reasoning in Language Models

author.name: Isha Puri, Mehul Damani, Idan Shenfeld, Marzyeh Ghassemi, Jacob Andreas, Yoon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes using RL to train language models that can generate multiple plausible hypotheses with calibrated confidence estimates, rather than collapsing to a single dominant answer. Addresses the problem of distributional reasoning for tasks with inherent ambiguity like medical diagnosis.

entry.title: Estimating near-verbatim extraction risk in language models with decoding-constrained beam search

author.name: A. Feder Cooper, Mark A. Lemley, Christopher De Sa, Lea Duesterwald, Allison Casasola, Jamie Hayes, Katherine Lee, Daniel E. Ho, Percy Liang

entry.summary: Introduces decoding-constrained beam search to efficiently estimate near-verbatim memorization extraction risk in LLMs, providing deterministic lower bounds much cheaper than Monte Carlo sampling (~100K samples). Addresses privacy and copyright risks from LLM memorization.

entry.title: WAFT-Stereo: Warping-Alone Field Transforms for Stereo Matching

author.name: Yihan Wang, Jia Deng

entry.summary: WAFT-Stereo demonstrates that cost volumes are unnecessary for strong stereo matching, replacing them with warping for improved efficiency. It ranks first on ETH3D, KITTI, and Middlebury benchmarks while being 1.8-6.7x faster than competitive methods, with 81% zero-shot error reduction on ETH3D.

entry.title: Test your best methods on our hard CoT interp tasks

author.name: daria

entry.summary: Introduces nine objective benchmark tasks for chain-of-thought interpretability where GPT 5.2 monitors fail out-of-distribution. Baselines probes and TF-IDF, finding they often outperform zero/few-shot LLM monitors OOD. From Neel Nanda's MATS program.

entry.title: Beyond Content Safety: Real-Time Monitoring for Reasoning Vulnerabilities in Large Language Models

author.name: Xunguang Wang, Yuguang Zhou, Qingyue Wang, Zongjie Li, Ruixuan Huang, Zhenlan Ji, Pingchuan Ma, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Identifies 'reasoning safety' as a new security dimension beyond content safety, proposing a nine-category taxonomy of unsafe reasoning behaviors in LLMs and developing real-time monitoring for chain-of-thought reasoning vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Closing the Confidence-Faithfulness Gap in Large Language Models

author.name: Miranda Muqing Miao, Lyle Ungar

entry.summary: Shows that calibration and verbalized confidence in LLMs are encoded linearly but orthogonally in representation space. Reasoning disrupts verbalized confidence, and steering vectors can partially close the confidence-faithfulness gap.

entry.title: R-C2: Cycle-Consistent Reinforcement Learning Improves Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Zirui Zhang, Haoyu Dong, Kexin Pei, Chengzhi Mao

entry.summary: R-C2 introduces cycle-consistent reinforcement learning for multimodal reasoning, using cross-modal backward-forward inference cycles as a dense, label-free reward signal to resolve internal model conflicts between visual and textual modalities.

entry.title: Shopping with a Platform AI Assistant: Who Adopts, When in the Journey, and What For

author.name: Se Yan (Zachary), Han Zhong (Zachary), Zemin (Zachary), Zhong, Wenyu Zhou

entry.summary: Large-scale study of 31 million users on Ctrip examining how consumers adopt platform-embedded shopping AI. Finds adoption is highest among older consumers and female users, reversing typical AI adoption demographics, and that AI chat interleaves with traditional search in purchase journeys.

entry.title: Imperative Interference: Social Register Shapes Instruction Topology in Large Language Models

author.name: Tony Mason

entry.summary: Discovers that LLM system prompt instructions that cooperate in English compete in Spanish due to social register differences in imperative mood. Declarative rewriting reduces cross-linguistic variance by 81%.

entry.title: Dispatch from Anthropic v. Department of War Preliminary Injunction Motion Hearing

author.name: Zack_M_Davis

entry.summary: A first-hand account of the preliminary injunction hearing in Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War, concerning a contract dispute where the government allegedly attempted to repurpose Anthropic's AI systems for military applications beyond the original agreement. The report covers legal arguments from both sides about contractual obligations, national security claims, and Anthropic's responsible scaling commitments.

entry.title: Cross-Model Disagreement as a Label-Free Correctness Signal

author.name: Matt Gorbett, Suman Jana

entry.summary: Introduces cross-model disagreement as a simple, training-free signal for detecting when LLMs are wrong, specifically targeting confident errors where a model is wrong but certain. Uses a second verifier model to compute surprise/uncertainty about the first model's answer.

entry.title: Mechanistically Interpreting Compression in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Veeraraju Elluru, Arth Singh, Roberto Aguero, Ajay Agarwal, Debojyoti Das, Hreetam Paul

entry.summary: Uses causal circuit analysis and crosscoder-based feature comparisons to examine how pruning and quantization change VLM internals. Finds pruning preserves circuit structure but rotates features, while quantization modifies circuits but keeps features better aligned. Introduces VLMSafe-420 safety benchmark.

entry.title: Formal Semantics for Agentic Tool Protocols: A Process Calculus Approach

author.name: Andreas Schlapbach

entry.summary: Provides the first process calculus formalization of Schema-Guided Dialogue (SGD) and Model Context Protocol (MCP), proving they are structurally bisimilar under a well-defined mapping but that the reverse mapping breaks symmetry, revealing fundamental differences.

entry.title: A Gait Foundation Model Predicts Multi-System Health Phenotypes from 3D Skeletal Motion

author.name: Adam Gabet, Sarah Kohn, Guy Lutsker, Shira Gelman, Anastasia Godneva, Gil Sasson, Arad Zulti, David Krongauz, Rotem Shaulitch, Assaf Rotem, Ohad Doron, Yuval Brodsky, Adina Weinberger, Eran Segal

entry.summary: Develops a gait foundation model from 3D skeletal motion data of 3,414 adults, showing learned embeddings predict age, BMI, visceral adipose tissue, and 1,980 of 3,210 phenotypic targets across 18 body systems, establishing gait as a systemic biomarker.

entry.title: TRAJEVAL: Decomposing Code Agent Trajectories for Fine-Grained Diagnosis

author.name: Myeongsoo Kim, Dingmin Wang, Siwei Cui, Farima Farmahinifarahani, Shweta Garg, Baishakhi Ray, Terry Yue Zhuo, Rajdeep Mukherjee, Varun Kumar

entry.summary: TRAJEVAL decomposes code agent trajectories into search, read, and edit stages for fine-grained diagnosis. Analysis of 16,758 trajectories reveals universal inefficiencies: all agents examine ~10x more files than needed, with specific failure patterns differing by architecture.

entry.title: Train at Moving Edge: Online-Verified Prompt Selection for Efficient RL Training of Large Reasoning Model

author.name: Jiahao Wu, Ning Lu, Shengcai Liu, Kun Wang, Yanting Yang, Li Qing, Ke Tang

entry.summary: Proposes online-verified prompt selection for efficient RL training of reasoning models, identifying that learning signals concentrate at the 'learning edge' (intersection of intermediate difficulty and high uncertainty) which shifts during training.

entry.title: Prune as You Generate: Online Rollout Pruning for Faster and Better RLVR

author.name: Haobo Xu, Sirui Chen, Ruizhong Qiu, Yuchen Yan, Chen Luo, Monica Cheng, Jingrui He, Hanghang Tong

entry.summary: Introduces arrol, an online rollout pruning method for RLVR that prunes rollouts during generation while steering surviving ones toward correctness-balanced distributions, improving both efficiency and learning signal quality.

entry.title: The Anatomy of Uncertainty in LLMs

author.name: Aditya Taparia, Ransalu Senanayake, Kowshik Thopalli, Vivek Narayanaswamy

entry.summary: Proposes decomposing LLM uncertainty into three semantic components: input ambiguity, knowledge gaps, and decoding randomness. Argues this provides more actionable insights than traditional aleatoric-epistemic decomposition for improving generative models.

entry.title: Malicious LLM-Based Conversational AI Makes Users Reveal Personal Information

author.name: Xiao Zhan, Juan Carlos Carrillo, William Seymour, Jose Such

entry.summary: Creates malicious LLM-based conversational AI systems deliberately designed to extract personal information from users through various disclosure strategies, and systematically investigates their effectiveness.

entry.title: Sparse Visual Thought Circuits in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yunpeng Zhou

entry.summary: Tests the modularity hypothesis in VLMs using sparse autoencoders, finding that while intervening on individual task-selective feature sets can improve reasoning, combining feature sets causes output drift and accuracy degradation due to shared internal pathways.

entry.title: SlopCodeBench: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Degrade Over Long-Horizon Iterative Tasks

author.name: Gabriel Orlanski, Devjeet Roy, Alexander Yun, Changho Shin, Alex Gu, Albert Ge, Dyah Adila, Frederic Sala, Aws Albarghouthi

entry.summary: SlopCodeBench evaluates how code agents degrade over iterative development, tracking verbosity and duplication as agents repeatedly extend their own solutions. Finds that code quality degrades predictably and impacts future extensibility.

entry.title: SEVerA: Verified Synthesis of Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Debangshu Banerjee, Changming Xu, Gagandeep Singh

entry.summary: Introduces SEVerA, a framework for self-evolving LLM agents with formal safety and correctness guarantees. Formulates agentic code generation as a constrained learning problem with Formally Guarded Generative Models (FGGM) combining hard specifications with soft objectives.

entry.title: FinMCP-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Real-World Financial Tool Use under the Model Context Protocol

author.name: Jie Zhu, Yimin Tian, Boyang Li, Kehao Wu, Zhongzhi Liang, Junhui Li, Xianyin Zhang, Lifan Guo, Feng Chen, Yong Liu, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: FinMCP-Bench benchmarks LLM agents on real-world financial tool use under the Model Context Protocol (MCP), with 613 samples across 10 scenarios and 65 real financial MCPs, evaluating single-tool, multi-tool, and multi-turn interactions.

entry.title: Model2Kernel: Model-Aware Symbolic Execution For Safe CUDA Kernels

author.name: Mengting He, Shihao Xia, Haomin Jia, Wenfei Wu, Linhai Song

entry.summary: Model2Kernel is the first symbolic execution tool for detecting CUDA memory bugs in LLM inference systems, addressing memory-safety vulnerabilities in GPU kernels that implement transformer operations.

entry.title: AIP: Agent Identity Protocol for Verifiable Delegation Across MCP and A2A

author.name: Sunil Prakash

entry.summary: Introduces Invocation-Bound Capability Tokens (IBCTs) for verifying AI agent identity across MCP and A2A protocols. Found that ~2,000 MCP servers lacked authentication, highlighting a critical infrastructure gap in agentic AI systems.

entry.title: The System Prompt Is the Attack Surface: How LLM Agent Configuration Shapes Security and Creates Exploitable Vulnerabilities

author.name: Ron Litvak

entry.summary: Presents PhishNChips, studying how system prompt configuration affects LLM email agent phishing detection. Shows a single model's phishing bypass rate ranges from <1% to 97% depending on prompt, revealing prompt-model interaction as a first-order security variable.

entry.title: How Pruning Reshapes Features: Sparse Autoencoder Analysis of Weight-Pruned Language Models

author.name: Hector Borobia, Elies Segu\'i-Mas, Guillermina Tormo-Carb\'o

entry.summary: First systematic study of how weight pruning reshapes LLM feature geometry using sparse autoencoders. Key finding: rare SAE features survive pruning far better than frequent ones across three model families and two pruning methods.

entry.title: Revisiting On-Policy Distillation: Empirical Failure Modes and Simple Fixes

author.name: Yuqian Fu, Haohuan Huang, Kaiwen Jiang, Yuanheng Zhu, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: Revisits on-policy distillation for LLM post-training, identifying failure modes where token-level OPD is biased relative to sequence-level reverse-KL. Provides theoretical analysis of the bias-variance tradeoff and proposes practical fixes for long-horizon settings.

entry.title: Amplified Patch-Level Differential Privacy for Free via Random Cropping

author.name: Kaan Durmaz, Jan Schuchardt, Sebastian Schmidt, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: Shows that random cropping as data augmentation provides an additional source of differential privacy amplification when sensitive content is spatially localized, complementing gradient noise and minibatch sampling. Formalizes this as 'patch-level DP'.

entry.title: The Order Is The Message

author.name: Jordan LeDoux

entry.summary: Demonstrates that training example ordering alone can determine whether neural networks generalize on modular arithmetic, with structured orderings achieving 99.5% accuracy while IID ordering achieves only 0.3%. The generalizing model constructs Fourier representations dual to the ordering structure.

entry.title: The Rules-and-Facts Model for Simultaneous Generalization and Memorization in Neural Networks

author.name: Gabriele Farn\'e, Fabrizio Boncoraglio, Lenka Zdeborov\'a

entry.summary: Introduces the Rules-and-Facts (RAF) model, a minimal solvable setting that characterizes how neural networks simultaneously learn generalizable rules and memorize specific exceptions. Bridges teacher-student frameworks with Gardner capacity analysis.

entry.title: MedOpenClaw: Auditable Medical Imaging Agents Reasoning over Uncurated Full Studies

author.name: Weixiang Shen, Yanzhu Hu, Che Liu, Junde Wu, Jiayuan Zhu, Chengzhi Shen, Min Xu, Yueming Jin, Benedikt Wiestler, Daniel Rueckert, Jiazhen Pan

entry.summary: Proposes MedOpenClaw, an auditable runtime for VLMs to operate within medical imaging tools like 3D Slicer, with MedFlowBench covering brain MRI and lung CT/PET for evaluating full-study clinical reasoning.

entry.title: MoE-GRPO: Optimizing Mixture-of-Experts via Reinforcement Learning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Dohwan Ko, Jinyoung Park, Seoung Choi, Sanghyeok Lee, Seohyun Lee, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: MoE-GRPO uses reinforcement learning (GRPO) to optimize expert routing in Mixture-of-Experts vision-language models, replacing deterministic top-K routing with RL-based selection for improved diversity and performance.

entry.title: HiSpatial: Taming Hierarchical 3D Spatial Understanding in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Huizhi Liang, Yichao Shen, Yu Deng, Sicheng Xu, Zhiyuan Feng, Tong Zhang, Yaobo Liang, Jiaolong Yang

entry.summary: HiSpatial decomposes 3D spatial understanding for VLMs into four hierarchical levels and constructs a large-scale pipeline processing ~5M images with 45M+ objects for 3D spatial VQA, incorporating RGB-D with metric-scale point maps.

entry.title: Load-Bearing Obfuscation and Self-Jailbreaking CoT

author.name: Graeme Ford

entry.summary: The author presents chain-of-thought traces from fine-tuned checkpoints of Kimi K2.5 that appear to show 'load-bearing obfuscation'—where the model's internal reasoning uses coded or indirect language that materially contributes to bypassing safety restrictions. The traces also demonstrate self-jailbreaking behavior where the model reasons its way around refusals during its thinking process.

entry.title: Training the Knowledge Base through Evidence Distillation and Write-Back Enrichment

author.name: Yuxing Lu, Xukai Zhao, Wei Wu, Jinzhuo Wang

entry.summary: WriteBack-RAG treats the knowledge base in RAG systems as a trainable component, using labeled examples to distill relevant documents into compact knowledge units that are indexed alongside the original corpus, improving retrieval quality across four RAG methods and six benchmarks.

entry.title: How Far Are Vision-Language Models from Constructing the Real World? A Benchmark for Physical Generative Reasoning

author.name: Luyu Yang, Yutong Dai, An Yan, Viraj Prabhu, Ran Xu, Zeyuan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces DreamHouse, a benchmark testing whether vision-language models can reason about physical construction processes, not just generate visually plausible outputs. Evaluates whether models grasp step-by-step processes and physical dependencies for design-to-construction pipelines.

entry.title: The Competence Shadow: Theory and Bounds of AI Assistance in Safety Engineering

author.name: Umair Siddique

entry.summary: Develops a formal framework for understanding how AI assistance in safety engineering can introduce systematic blind spots ('competence shadows'). Formalizes safety competence as five-dimensional and argues why safety engineering resists benchmark-driven evaluation.

entry.title: Do LLMs Know What They Know? Measuring Metacognitive Efficiency with Signal Detection Theory

author.name: Jon-Paul Cacioli

entry.summary: Applies Signal Detection Theory (Type-2 meta-d') to measure LLM metacognitive efficiency, separating what models know from how well they know what they know. Finds metacognitive efficiency varies substantially even when knowledge is similar.

entry.title: PackForcing: Short Video Training Suffices for Long Video Sampling and Long Context Inference

author.name: Xiaofeng Mao, Shaohao Rui, Kaining Ying, Bo Zheng, Chuanhao Li, Mingmin Chi, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: Presents PackForcing, a framework for autoregressive video diffusion that manages generation history through a three-partition KV-cache strategy (Sink/Mid/Refresh tokens), achieving 32x token reduction for mid-range context while maintaining quality.

entry.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Step Tool Orchestration with Constrained Data Synthesis and Graduated Rewards

author.name: Cheng Jiayang, Xin Liu, Zhihan Zhang, Haoyang Wen, Zixuan Zhang, Qingyu Yin, Shiyang Li, Priyanka Nigam, Bing Yin, Chao Zhang, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Presents a framework for training LLMs on multi-step tool orchestration using a large-scale cache of real API responses for RL environment construction and graduated rewards for partial correctness. Addresses the challenge of multi-dependent API calls.

entry.title: LanteRn: Latent Visual Structured Reasoning

author.name: Andr\'e G. Viveiros, Nuno Gon\c{c}alves, Matthias Lindemann, Andr\'e Martins

entry.summary: Introduces LanteRn, a framework enabling large multimodal models to interleave language with compact latent visual representations for visual reasoning directly in latent space, avoiding expensive pixel-space computation.

entry.title: Bridging Perception and Reasoning: Token Reweighting for RLVR in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Jinda Lu, Junkang Wu, Jinghan Li, Kexin Huang, Shuo Yang, Guoyin Wang, Jiancan Wu, Xiang Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: Proposes Token-Reweighting (ToR) for RLVR in multimodal LLMs, finding that perception and reasoning tokens are interdependent and that differentially weighting them improves RL training for visual reasoning.

entry.title: Trust as Monitoring: Evolutionary Dynamics of User Trust and AI Developer Behaviour

author.name: Adeela Bashir, Zhao Song, Ndidi Bianca Ogbo, Nataliya Balabanova, Martin Smit, Chin-wing Leung, Paolo Bova, Manuel Chica Serrano, Dhanushka Dissanayake, Manh Hong Duong, Elias Fernandez Domingos, Nikita Huber-Kralj, Marcus Krellner, Andrew Powell, Stefan Sarkadi, Fernando P. Santos, Zia Ush Shamszaman, Chaimaa Tarzi, Paolo Turrini, Grace Ibukunoluwa Ufeoshi, Victor A. Vargas-Perez, Alessandro Di Stefano, Simon T. Powers, The Anh Han

entry.summary: Models AI safety as an evolutionary game between users and developers, treating user trust as reduced monitoring in repeated interactions. Uses evolutionary game theory to study how trust strategies and developer compliance co-evolve under different institutional regimes.

entry.title: Rethinking Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark and Evaluation

author.name: Yeonjun In, Mehrab Tanjim, Jayakumar Subramanian, Sungchul Kim, Uttaran Bhattacharya, Wonjoong Kim, Sangwu Park, Somdeb Sarkhel, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: Proposes multi-perspective failure attribution for multi-agent systems, introducing MP-Bench, the first benchmark accounting for attribution ambiguity when failures have multiple plausible root causes due to complex inter-agent dependencies.

entry.title: Back to Basics: Revisiting ASR in the Age of Voice Agents

author.name: Geeyang Tay, Wentao Ma, Jaewon Lee, Yuzhi Tang, Daniel Lee, Weisu Yin, Dongming Shen, Silin Meng, Yi Zhu, Mu Li, Alex Smola

entry.summary: Introduces WildASR, a multilingual diagnostic benchmark for ASR robustness that factorizes performance along environmental degradation, demographic shift, and linguistic diversity axes. Finds severe and uneven degradation across seven widely-used ASR systems.

entry.title: Grokking as a Falsifiable Finite-Size Transition

author.name: Yuda Bi, Chenyu Zhang, Qiheng Wang, Vince D Calhoun

entry.summary: Treats grokking as a falsifiable finite-size phase transition by using group order as an extensive variable and applying condensed-matter diagnostic methods, strongly disfavoring a smooth-crossover interpretation.

entry.title: CRAFT: Grounded Multi-Agent Coordination Under Partial Information

author.name: Abhijnan Nath, Hannah VanderHoeven, Nikhil Krishnaswamy

entry.summary: Introduces CRAFT, a multi-agent benchmark for pragmatic communication under partial information where agents with complementary views must coordinate to construct shared 3D structures. Tests spatial grounding, belief modeling, and pragmatic communication.

entry.title: Shape and Substance: Dual-Layer Side-Channel Attacks on Local Vision-Language Models

author.name: Eyal Hadad, Mordechai Guri

entry.summary: Demonstrates a dual-layer side-channel attack on local VLMs exploiting Dynamic High-Resolution preprocessing (e.g., AnyRes) that creates workload-dependent inputs, enabling fingerprinting of input geometry and semantic content.

entry.title: Out of Sight but Not Out of Mind: Hybrid Memory for Dynamic Video World Models

author.name: Kaijin Chen, Dingkang Liang, Xin Zhou, Yikang Ding, Xiaoqiang Liu, Pengfei Wan, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: Introduces Hybrid Memory for video world models, enabling models to track dynamic subjects that temporarily disappear and re-emerge. Constructs HM-World, a 59K-clip dataset with decoupled camera and subject motion for evaluating this capability.

entry.title: Can LLMs Beat Classical Hyperparameter Optimization Algorithms? A Study on autoresearch

author.name: Fabio Ferreira, Lucca Wobbe, Arjun Krishnakumar, Frank Hutter, Arber Zela

entry.summary: Compares LLM-based hyperparameter optimization agents against classical HPO algorithms (CMA-ES, TPE) using the autoresearch framework. Classical methods outperform in fixed search spaces, but LLMs narrow the gap substantially when allowed to edit training code directly.

entry.title: Light Cones For Vision: Simple Causal Priors For Visual Hierarchy

author.name: Manglam Kartik, Neel Tushar Shah

entry.summary: Introduces Worldline Slot Attention, modeling objects as persistent spacetime trajectories with Lorentzian geometry to capture visual hierarchy (parts within wholes). Lorentzian worldlines achieve 6x improvement over Euclidean baselines for hierarchy-level accuracy.

entry.title: On Neural Scaling Laws for Weather Emulation through Continual Training

author.name: Shashank Subramanian, Alexander Kiefer, Arnur Nigmetov, Amir Gholami, Dmitriy Morozov, Michael W. Mahoney

entry.summary: Studies neural scaling laws for weather forecasting models using Swin Transformers with continual training and periodic cooldowns. Shows models follow predictable scaling trends and can outperform standard cosine learning rate schedules.

entry.title: Enabling ab initio geometry optimization of strongly correlated systems with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo

author.name: P. Bern\'at Szab\'o, Zeno Sch\"atzle, Frank No\'e

entry.summary: Presents a framework combining transferable deep-learning variational Monte Carlo with efficient energy, force, and Hessian estimation for ab initio geometry optimization of strongly correlated molecular systems. Frank Noé is a notable author.

entry.title: Large Language Model as Token Compressor and Decompressor

author.name: Wenbing Li, Zikai Song, Jielei Zhang, Tianhao Zhao, Junkai Lin, Yiran Wang, Wei Yang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLMs can function as token compressors/decompressors, fine-tuning a pretrained LLM to translate text into compact discrete Z-tokens achieving up to 18x token reduction while maintaining reconstruction quality.

entry.title: From Weights to Concepts: Data-Free Interpretability of CLIP via Singular Vector Decomposition

author.name: Francesco Gentile, Nicola Dall'Asen, Francesco Tonini, Massimiliano Mancini, Lorenzo Vaquero, Elisa Ricci

entry.summary: Introduces SITH, a fully data-free, training-free framework for interpreting CLIP's vision transformer by decomposing attention head weight matrices via singular vectors and explaining them as sparse concept combinations.

entry.title: AVControl: Efficient Framework for Training Audio-Visual Controls

author.name: Matan Ben-Yosef, Tavi Halperin, Naomi Ken Korem, Mohammad Salama, Harel Cain, Asaf Joseph, Anthony Chen, Urska Jelercic, Ofir Bibi

entry.summary: AVControl introduces a lightweight, extendable framework for controlling audio-visual generation built on the LTX-2 foundation model, where each control modality is trained as a separate LoRA on a parallel canvas. This avoids monolithic multi-control models or costly architectural changes.

entry.title: VideoTIR: Accurate Understanding for Long Videos with Efficient Tool-Integrated Reasoning

author.name: Zhe Gao, Shiyu Shen, Taifeng Chai, Weinong Wang, Haotian Xu, Xing W, Wenbin Li, Qi Fan, Yang Gao, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: VideoTIR uses reinforcement learning to train MLLMs for proper tool usage in long video understanding, addressing hallucination problems caused by token imbalance between text and visual modalities.

entry.title: Visual Attention Drifts,but Anchors Hold:Mitigating Hallucination in Multimodal Large Language Models via Cross-Layer Visual Anchors

author.name: Chengxu Yang, Jingling Yuan, Chuang Hu, Jiawei Jiang

entry.summary: CLVA discovers that hallucination in MLLMs stems from deep-layer attention regressing toward initial visual noise, and proposes reinforcing mid-layer visual anchors as a training-free mitigation.

entry.title: MSRL: Scaling Generative Multimodal Reward Modeling via Multi-Stage Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenglong Wang, Yifu Huo, Yang Gan, Qiaozhi He, Qi Meng, Bei Li, Yan Wang, Junfu Liu, Tianhua Zhou, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: MSRL proposes multi-stage reinforcement learning for scaling multimodal reward models, first learning generalizable reward reasoning from text-only data then transferring to multimodal settings.

entry.title: SportSkills: Physical Skill Learning from Sports Instructional Videos

author.name: Kumar Ashutosh, Chi Hsuan Wu, Kristen Grauman

entry.summary: SportSkills introduces the first large-scale sports dataset (360K videos, 55 sports) for physical skill learning, showing that fine-grained sports understanding enables 4x representation gains over standard activity datasets.

entry.title: MACRO: Advancing Multi-Reference Image Generation with Structured Long-Context Data

author.name: Zhekai Chen, Yuqing Wang, Manyuan Zhang, Xihui Liu

entry.summary: MACRO introduces MacroData (400K samples with up to 10 references) for multi-reference image generation and a structured long-context training approach across customization, illustration, spatial reasoning, and view synthesis.

entry.title: LaMP: Learning Vision-Language-Action Policies with 3D Scene Flow as Latent Motion Prior

author.name: Xinkai Wang, Chenyi Wang, Yifu Xu, Mingzhe Ye, Fu-Cheng Zhang, Jialin Tian, Xinyu Zhan, Lifeng Zhu, Cewu Lu, Lixin Yang

entry.summary: LaMP embeds dense 3D scene flow as a latent motion prior in a VLA framework for robotic manipulation, using a Motion Expert to condition action prediction through gated cross-attention.

entry.title: RubricEval: A Rubric-Level Meta-Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Judges in Instruction Following

author.name: Tianjun Pan, Xuan Lin, Wenyan Yang, Qianyu He, Shisong Chen, Licai Qi, Wanqing Xu, Hongwei Feng, Bo Xu, Yanghua Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces RubricEval, the first rubric-level meta-evaluation benchmark for LLM judges in instruction following, with 3,486 quality-controlled instances and Easy/Hard subsets to assess fine-grained judgment accuracy.

entry.title: On the Foundations of Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence

author.name: TJ Dunham

entry.summary: Formalizes a 'Determinism Thesis' for trustworthy AI, proving that platform-deterministic inference is necessary and sufficient for verification. Constructs a pure integer inference engine achieving bitwise identical output across ARM and x86 architectures.

entry.title: X-OPD: Cross-Modal On-Policy Distillation for Capability Alignment in Speech LLMs

author.name: Di Cao, Dongjie Fu, Hai Yu, Siqi Zheng, Xu Tan, Tao Jin

entry.summary: X-OPD proposes cross-modal on-policy distillation to align speech LLM capabilities with text-based counterparts, using on-policy rollouts evaluated by a text-based teacher model to provide token-level feedback.

entry.title: ReLope: KL-Regularized LoRA Probes for Multimodal LLM Routing

author.name: Yaopei Zeng, Congchao Wang, Blake JianHang Chen, Lu Lin

entry.summary: Introduces ReLope, KL-regularized LoRA probes for routing between lightweight and expensive multimodal LLMs. Identifies that visual inputs weaken correctness signal separability in hidden states and proposes complementary approaches to improve probe routing for MLLMs.

entry.title: Trace2Skill: Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills

author.name: Jingwei Ni, Yihao Liu, Xinpeng Liu, Yutao Sun, Mengyu Zhou, Pengyu Cheng, Dexin Wang, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Trace2Skill distills domain-specific skills for LLM agents from execution trajectories by dispatching parallel sub-agents to analyze diverse experiences before synthesizing comprehensive skill guides, mimicking how human experts author skills.

entry.title: Agent Factories for High Level Synthesis: How Far Can General-Purpose Coding Agents Go in Hardware Optimization?

author.name: Abhishek Bhandwaldar, Mihir Choudhury, Ruchir Puri, Akash Srivastava

entry.summary: Presents an agent factory for high-level synthesis hardware optimization, using a two-stage pipeline where general-purpose coding agents decompose designs, optimize sub-kernels, and assemble solutions via integer linear programming.

entry.title: When Consistency Becomes Bias: Interviewer Effects in Semi-Structured Clinical Interviews

author.name: Hasindri Watawana, Sergio Burdisso, Diego A. Moreno-Galv\'an, Fernando S\'anchez-Vega, A. Pastor L\'opez-Monroy, Petr Motlicek, Esa\'u Villatoro-Tello

entry.summary: Identifies systematic bias in automatic depression detection from clinical interviews: models exploit interviewer prompts rather than patient language. Restricting to participant utterances reveals that high scores were artifacts of interview structure.

entry.title: Self-Corrected Image Generation with Explainable Latent Rewards

author.name: Yinyi Luo, Hrishikesh Gokhale, Marios Savvides, Jindong Wang, Shengfeng He

entry.summary: Proposes xLARD, a self-correcting text-to-image generation framework that uses multimodal LLMs to provide explainable latent rewards, guiding a lightweight corrector to refine latent representations based on structured feedback.

entry.title: Efficient Detection of Bad Benchmark Items with Novel Scalability Coefficients

author.name: Michael Hardy, Joshua Gilbert, Benjamin Domingue

entry.summary: Introduces nonparametric scalability coefficients based on isotonic regression for efficiently detecting bad items in large-scale benchmarks. The signed isotonic R² measures inter-item consistency to flag problematic questions.

entry.title: Pixelis: Reasoning in Pixels, from Seeing to Acting

author.name: Yunpeng Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Pixelis, a pixel-space agent that operates directly on images/videos via executable operations and learns from consequences through three training phases: supervised fine-tuning, rule-based RL, and test-time self-refinement.

entry.title: Vision Hopfield Memory Networks

author.name: Jianfeng Wang, Amine M'Charrak, Luk Koska, Xiangtao Wang, Daniel Petriceanu, Mykyta Smyrnov, Ruizhi Wang, Michael Bumbar, Luca Pinchetti, Thomas Lukasiewicz

entry.summary: Proposes Vision Hopfield Memory Network (V-HMN), a brain-inspired vision backbone integrating hierarchical Hopfield memory dynamics with iterative refinement at local and global levels for improved interpretability.
