entry.title: PP-OCRv5: A Specialized 5M-Parameter Model Rivaling Billion-Parameter Vision-Language Models on OCR Tasks

author.name: Cheng Cui, Yubo Zhang, Ting Sun, Xueqing Wang, Hongen Liu, Manhui Lin, Yue Zhang, Tingquan Gao, Changda Zhou, Jiaxuan Liu, Zelun Zhang, Jing Zhang, Jun Zhang, Yi Liu

entry.summary: Introduces PP-OCRv5, a lightweight 5M-parameter OCR system that achieves performance competitive with billion-parameter vision-language models while offering better localization precision and fewer hallucinations. Challenges the assumption that model scale is necessary for high OCR accuracy.

entry.title: Bridging the Know-Act Gap via Task-Level Autoregressive Reasoning

author.name: Jihyun Janice Ahn, Ryo Kamoi, Berk Atil, Renze Lou, WonWoo Kang, Heehyun Park, Sarkar Snigdha Sarathi Das, Zhuoyang Zou, Xiaoxin Lu, Yusen Zhang, Asfahan Shah, Ridwanul Hasan Tanvir, Lingxiao Zhao, Hongxi Huang, Vignesh Venkatesh, Dianjun Lin, Hamid Shah, Wentao Wang, Zhanpeng Song, Joshua Reed Bassin, Dax Patel, Ishan Appareddy Agrahar, Sahil Pardasani, Xin Dong, Fatemeh Rahbari, Benjamin David Rishel, Soochan Andrew Lee, Yuv Boghani, Ali B. AlNaseeb, Pranav Suby, Seokhyeon Bae, Shreya Buddharaju, Damien Kula, Soumyadeep Das, Hanyang Frank Liu, Faye Mo, Wenpeng Yin

entry.summary: Identifies a 'know-act gap' where LLMs can discriminatively recognize flawed inputs but fail to reflect this in generative responses. Introduces FaultyScience benchmark and proposes task-level autoregressive reasoning (TAR) to bridge the gap.

entry.title: Graph Signal Processing Meets Mamba2: Adaptive Filter Bank via Delta Modulation

author.name: Yehjin Shin, Seojin Kim, Noseong Park

entry.summary: Proposes HADES, a Graph Signal Processing framework that reinterprets Mamba2's multi-head recurrence as an adaptive filter bank on a line graph, introducing shared filters for global low-pass and expert filters for local high-pass behavior in a hierarchical architecture.

entry.title: KALAVAI: Predicting When Independent Specialist Fusion Works -- A Quantitative Model for Post-Hoc Cooperative LLM Training

author.name: Ramchand Kumaresan

entry.summary: Shows that independently trained domain specialist LLMs can be fused post-hoc with predictable gains (gain = 0.82 × divergence - 2.72, R²=0.856), enabling practitioners to estimate cooperative value before committing compute. Demonstrates consistent gains across model scales.

entry.title: Robust Safety Monitoring of Language Models via Activation Watermarking

author.name: Toluwani Aremu, Daniil Ognev, Samuele Poppi, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: Proposes activation watermarking for robust safety monitoring of LLMs, formulated as a security game where adversaries try to evade detection while eliciting unsafe behavior. Aims to make monitors robust against adaptive attackers.

entry.title: SortedRL: Accelerating RL Training for LLMs through Online Length-Aware Scheduling

author.name: Yiqi Zhang, Huiqiang Jiang, Xufang Luo, Zhihe Yang, Chengruidong Zhang, Yifei Shen, Dongsheng Li, Yuqing Yang, Lili Qiu, Yang You

entry.summary: Proposes SortedRL, an online length-aware scheduling strategy for RL training of LLMs that reorders rollout samples by output length to improve efficiency and reduce synchronization overhead in long chain-of-thought generation.

entry.title: MedObvious: Exposing the Medical Moravec's Paradox in VLMs via Clinical Triage

author.name: Ufaq Khan, Umair Nawaz, L D M S S Teja, Numaan Saeed, Muhammad Bilal, Yutong Xie, Mohammad Yaqub, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: Introduces MedObvious, a benchmark exposing the 'Medical Moravec's Paradox' where VLMs can generate plausible diagnostic narratives even when input images are invalid, inconsistent, or from wrong modalities.

entry.title: Likelihood hacking in probabilistic program synthesis

author.name: Jacek Karwowski, Younesse Kaddar, Zihuiwen Ye, Nikolay Malkin, Sam Staton

entry.summary: Formalizes 'likelihood hacking' in probabilistic program synthesis where RL-trained LLMs produce programs with unnormalized distributions to inflate reward, and proves a safe language fragment prevents this failure.

entry.title: A Deep Dive into Scaling RL for Code Generation with Synthetic Data and Curricula

author.name: Cansu Sancaktar, David Zhang, Gabriel Synnaeve, Taco Cohen

entry.summary: Introduces a scalable multi-turn synthetic data generation pipeline for RL training of code LLMs, where a teacher model iteratively refines problem difficulty based on student performance summaries. Shows curriculum and data diversity are more important than volume.

entry.title: Wasserstein Parallel Transport for Predicting the Dynamics of Statistical Systems

author.name: Tristan Luca Saidi, Gonzalo Mena, Larry Wasserman, Florian Gunsilius

entry.summary: Introduces 'Wasserstein Parallel Trends' for predicting dynamics of distributional systems using parallel transport along optimal transport geodesics, replacing vector subtraction with geodesic parallel transport for causal inference on distributions.

entry.title: Prompt Compression in Production Task Orchestration: A Pre-Registered Randomized Trial

author.name: Warren Johnson, Charles Lee

entry.summary: A pre-registered randomized controlled trial evaluating prompt compression on production multi-agent task orchestration with 358 Claude Sonnet 4.5 runs. It examines how compression changes output length (priced higher than input) across uniform and structure-aware strategies. Moderate compression (r=0.5) reduced total cost while aggressive compression had diminishing returns.

entry.title: Understanding LLM Performance Degradation in Multi-Instance Processing: The Roles of Instance Count and Context Length

author.name: Jingxuan Chen, Mohammad Taher Pilehvar, Jose Camacho-Collados

entry.summary: Comprehensively evaluates how LLMs degrade when processing multiple instances simultaneously, finding slight degradation for small counts but dramatic collapse beyond a threshold. Disentangles effects of instance count from context length.

entry.title: Bilevel Autoresearch: Meta-Autoresearching Itself

author.name: Yaonan Qu, Meng Lu

entry.summary: Introduces Bilevel Autoresearch where an outer loop meta-optimizes the inner autoresearch loop by generating and injecting new search mechanisms as Python code at runtime. Takes autoresearch literally—using autoresearch to optimize autoresearch.

entry.title: Mecha-nudges for Machines

author.name: Giulio Frey, Kawin Ethayarajh

entry.summary: Introduces mecha-nudges: changes to choice presentation that systematically influence AI agents without degrading the environment for humans. Formalizes using Bayesian persuasion with V-usable information for a common comparison scale.

entry.title: Whether, Not Which: Mechanistic Interpretability Reveals Dissociable Affect Reception and Emotion Categorization in LLMs

author.name: Michael Keeman

entry.summary: Tests emotion circuit claims in LLMs using clinical vignettes without emotion keywords, finding dissociable affect reception and emotion categorization. First clinical validity test using mechanistic interpretability grounded in clinical psychology.

entry.title: Conformal Risk Control for Safety-Critical Wildfire Evacuation Mapping: A Comparative Study of Tabular, Spatial, and Graph-Based Models

author.name: Baljinnyam Dayan

entry.summary: First application of conformal risk control (CRC) to wildfire spread prediction, providing formal finite-sample guarantees on false negative rate (FNR ≤ 0.05) for evacuation safety. Reveals that uncalibrated models at standard thresholds miss up to dangerous amounts of fire spread.

entry.title: WIST: Web-Grounded Iterative Self-Play Tree for Domain-Targeted Reasoning Improvement

author.name: Fangyuan Li, Pengfei Li, Shijie Wang, Junqi Gao, Jianxing Liu, Biqing Qi, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: Presents WIST, a framework for domain-targeted reasoning improvement that learns from the open web without curated corpora, using web-grounded iterative self-play with a domain tree for exploration and Challenger-Solver dynamics with RLVR.

entry.title: Tiny Inference-Time Scaling with Latent Verifiers

author.name: Davide Bucciarelli, Evelyn Turri, Lorenzo Baraldi, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi, Rita Cucchiara

entry.summary: Proposes VHS (Verifier on Hidden States), a lightweight verifier for inference-time scaling of diffusion models that operates directly on intermediate DiT hidden representations, avoiding costly pixel-space decoding and re-encoding required by MLLM verifiers.

entry.title: Agent Audit: A Security Analysis System for LLM Agent Applications

author.name: Haiyue Zhang, Yi Nian, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: Presents Agent Audit, a security analysis system for LLM agent applications that analyzes Python code and deployment artifacts through agent-aware dataflow analysis, credential detection, and MCP privilege-risk checks.

entry.title: Grounding Sim-to-Real Generalization in Dexterous Manipulation: An Empirical Study with Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ruixing Jin, Zicheng Zhu, Ruixiang Ouyang, Sheng Xu, Bo Yue, Zhizheng Wu, Guiliang Liu

entry.summary: Empirically examines sim-to-real transfer for dexterous manipulation with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models across four dimensions. Provides systematic analysis of what drives successful sim-to-real generalization for generalist manipulation policies.

entry.title: A Sobering Look at Tabular Data Generation via Probabilistic Circuits

author.name: Davide Scassola, Dylan Ponsford, Adri\'an Javaloy, Sebastiano Saccani, Luca Bortolussi, Henry Gouk, Antonio Vergari

entry.summary: Questions perceived progress in tabular data generation by highlighting evaluation limitations, then shows that simple probabilistic circuits match or beat state-of-the-art diffusion models at a fraction of the cost.

entry.title: VISion On Request: Enhanced VLLM efficiency with sparse, dynamically selected, vision-language interactions

author.name: Adrian Bulat, Alberto Baldrati, Ioannis Maniadis Metaxas, Yassine Ouali, Georgios Tzimiropoulos

entry.summary: Introduces VISOR, a method that improves LVLM efficiency by sparsifying vision-language token interactions rather than discarding visual tokens, avoiding the information bottleneck of token reduction approaches.

entry.title: Steering Code LLMs with Activation Directions for Language and Library Control

author.name: Md Mahbubur Rahman, Arjun Guha, Harshitha Menon

entry.summary: Investigates whether code LLM preferences for programming languages/libraries are encoded as linear directions in activation space that can be manipulated via steering vectors at inference time. Shows these interventions can override even explicit prompt instructions.

entry.title: HDPO: Hybrid Distillation Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation

author.name: Ken Ding

entry.summary: Introduces HDPO, which addresses the vanishing gradient problem in RL for math reasoning on problems the model can never solve ('cliff prompts') by using privileged self-distillation where the same model gets ground-truth hints to generate teacher rollouts.

entry.title: Scaling Recurrence-aware Foundation Models for Clinical Records via Next-Visit Prediction

author.name: Haresh Rengaraj Rajamohan, Xiang Gao, Weicheng Zhu, Shih-Lun Huang, Long Chen, Gabe Schulman, Huizhen Jin, Shengduo Li, Yixuan Wang, Huidi Yang, Kyunghyun Cho, Cem M. Deniz, Narges Razavian

entry.summary: RAVEN is a generative pretraining strategy for sequential EHR data that predicts next-visit clinical events autoregressively. It identifies a critical evaluation pitfall where repeated event tokens inflate metrics and introduces regularization to address this.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Medical Image Representation Learning

author.name: Philipp Wesp, Robbie Holland, Vasiliki Sideri-Lampretsa, Sergios Gatidis

entry.summary: Investigates sparse autoencoders for making medical imaging foundation model representations interpretable, showing that 10 sparse features can recover up to 87.8% of downstream performance with 99.4% dimensionality reduction.

entry.title: BeliefShift: Benchmarking Temporal Belief Consistency and Opinion Drift in LLM Agents

author.name: Praveen Kumar Myakala, Manan Agrawal, Rahul Manche

entry.summary: BeliefShift introduces a longitudinal benchmark for evaluating belief dynamics in multi-session LLM interactions, covering temporal belief consistency, contradiction detection, and evidence-driven revision. Includes 2,400 human-annotated trajectories spanning health, politics, personal values, and product preferences.

entry.title: Schema on the Inside: A Two-Phase Fine-Tuning Method for High-Efficiency Text-to-SQL at Scale

author.name: Chinmay Soni, Shivam Chourasia, Gaurav Kumar, Hitesh Kapoor

entry.summary: Presents a two-phase fine-tuning method for Text-to-SQL that internalizes the entire database schema, reducing input tokens by over 99% (from 17k to <100). Deployed for CriQ, a sister app to Dream11 with 250M users for cricket statistics queries.

entry.title: Comparing Developer and LLM Biases in Code Evaluation

author.name: Aditya Mittal, Ryan Shar, Zichu Wu, Shyam Agarwal, Tongshuang Wu, Chris Donahue, Ameet Talwalkar, Wayne Chi, Valerie Chen

entry.summary: TRACE evaluates LLM judges' ability to predict human preferences in code evaluation across chat programming, IDE autocompletion, and code editing. Best judges underperform human annotators by 12-23%. Identifies 35 significant sources of misalignment between LLM judges and developers.

entry.title: When Understanding Becomes a Risk: Authenticity and Safety Risks in the Emerging Image Generation Paradigm

author.name: Ye Leng, Junjie Chu, Mingjie Li, Chenhao Lin, Chao Shen, Michael Backes, Yun Shen, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Systematically compares safety risks of MLLMs vs diffusion models for image generation, finding MLLMs generate more unsafe images and more convincing deepfakes due to stronger semantic understanding capabilities.

entry.title: OmniWeaving: Towards Unified Video Generation with Free-form Composition and Reasoning

author.name: Kaihang Pan, Qi Tian, Jianwei Zhang, Weijie Kong, Jiangfeng Xiong, Yanxin Long, Shixue Zhang, Haiyi Qiu, Tan Wang, Zheqi Lv, Yue Wu, Liefeng Bo, Siliang Tang, Zhao Zhong

entry.summary: Proposes OmniWeaving, an open-source omni-level video generation model that handles interleaved text, multi-image, and video inputs with compositional and reasoning-informed capabilities, aiming to close the gap with proprietary systems like Seedance-2.0.

entry.title: Claude Code, Cowork and Codex #6: Claude Code Auto Use and Full Cowork Computer Use

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed coverage of major Anthropic agentic coding updates: Claude Code now has 'auto mode' where a classifier pre-approves safe commands, Claude Cowork can use keyboard and mouse for full computer access, and a new Dispatch feature lets users command agents from mobile via Telegram/Discord. Described as significant quality-of-life improvements for agentic coding workflows.

entry.title: EVA: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for End-to-End Video Agent

author.name: Yaolun Zhang, Ruohui Wang, Jiahao Wang, Yepeng Tang, Xuanyu Zheng, Haonan Duan, Hao Lu, Hanming Deng, Lewei Lu

entry.summary: Presents EVA, an RL framework for video understanding that enables planning-before-perception through iterative reasoning. The agent autonomously decides what to watch and when to answer, rather than processing entire videos.

entry.title: Improving Safety Alignment via Balanced Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Shiji Zhao, Mengyang Wang, Shukun Xiong, Fangzhou Chen, Qihui Zhu, Shouwei Ruan, Yisong Xiao, Ranjie Duan, Xun Chen, XingXing Wei

entry.summary: Addresses safety alignment overfitting in DPO by identifying 'Imbalanced Preference Comprehension' between responses in preference pairs. Proposes balanced DPO to improve safety alignment without the typical performance degradation.

entry.title: LLMON: An LLM-native Markup Language to Leverage Structure and Semantics at the LLM Interface

author.name: Michael Hind, Basel Shbita, Bo Wu, Farhan Ahmed, Chad DeLuca, Nathan Fulton, David Cox, Dan Gutfreund

entry.summary: Introduces LLMON (LLM Object Notation), a markup language that distinguishes between instructions and data in LLM prompts to reduce model confusion and mitigate prompt injection attacks by conveying structure and semantic metadata.

entry.title: Graph Energy Matching: Transport-Aligned Energy-Based Modeling for Graph Generation

author.name: Michal Balcerak, Suprosana Shit, Chinmay Prabhakar, Sebastian Kaltenbach, Michael S. Albergo, Yilun Du, Bjoern Menze

entry.summary: Introduces Graph Energy Matching (GEM), combining energy-based models with transport map optimization for graph generation, closing the fidelity gap between energy-based and diffusion models for discrete graphs.

entry.title: Perturbation: A simple and efficient adversarial tracer for representation learning in language models

author.name: Joshua Rozner, Cory Shain

entry.summary: Proposes 'Perturbation' - fine-tuning an LM on a single adversarial example and measuring how the perturbation spreads to other examples - as a method for studying linguistic representations without geometric assumptions.

entry.title: Qworld: Question-Specific Evaluation Criteria for LLMs

author.name: Shanghua Gao, Yuchang Su, Pengwei Sui, Curtis Ginder, Marinka Zitnik

entry.summary: Qworld introduces question-specific evaluation criteria for LLMs using a recursive expansion tree that decomposes questions into scenarios, perspectives, and fine-grained binary criteria. This moves beyond static rubrics and binary scores for evaluating open-ended LLM responses. The method generates context-dependent evaluation standards for each question.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Correctness: Scaling Evaluation of Long-Horizon Agents on Subjective Enterprise Tasks

author.name: Abhishek Chandwani, Ishan Gupta

entry.summary: Introduces LH-Bench for evaluating autonomous agents on subjective, long-horizon enterprise tasks, moving beyond binary correctness to expert-grounded rubrics and curated ground-truth artifacts for stepwise reward signals.

entry.title: Chain-of-Authorization: Internalizing Authorization into Large Language Models via Reasoning Trajectories

author.name: Yang Li, Yule Liu, Xinlei He, Youjian Zhao, Qi Li, Ke Xu

entry.summary: Proposes Chain-of-Authorization (CoA), internalizing access control into LLM reasoning via supervised training on authorization reasoning trajectories. Addresses the lack of inherent knowledge ownership awareness in LLMs.

entry.title: MemCollab: Cross-Agent Memory Collaboration via Contrastive Trajectory Distillation

author.name: Yurui Chang, Yiran Wu, Qingyun Wu, Lu Lin

entry.summary: Proposes MemCollab, a collaborative memory framework that constructs agent-agnostic memory by contrasting reasoning trajectories from different agents, enabling memory sharing across heterogeneous LLM agents.

entry.title: LLM Olympiad: Why Model Evaluation Needs a Sealed Exam

author.name: Jan Christian Blaise Cruz, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: Argues for Olympiad-style LLM evaluation events with sealed problems, frozen submissions, and standardized harnesses to combat benchmark-chasing and hidden evaluation choices. Proposes practical design for reproducible, auditable evaluation.

entry.title: Between the Layers Lies the Truth: Uncertainty Estimation in LLMs Using Intra-Layer Local Information Scores

author.name: Zvi N. Badash, Yonatan Belinkov, Moti Freiman

entry.summary: Proposes a compact uncertainty estimation method scoring cross-layer agreement patterns in LLM internal representations using a single forward pass. Matches probing in-distribution and outperforms it under cross-dataset transfer and quantization.

entry.title: First-Mover Bias in Gradient Boosting Explanations: Mechanism, Detection, and Resolution

author.name: Drake Caraker, Bryan Arnold, David Rhoads

entry.summary: Identifies and characterizes 'first-mover bias' in gradient boosting - a path-dependent concentration of feature importance where the first-selected correlated feature gains a self-reinforcing advantage through modified residuals, causing unstable SHAP rankings.

entry.title: FAAR: Format-Aware Adaptive Rounding for NVFP4

author.name: Hanglin Li, Shuchang Tian, Chen Lin, Zhiyong Zhao, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes FAAR, a learnable rounding strategy specifically designed for the NVFP4 format that accounts for its non-uniform numerical grid, improving ultra-low-bit quantization for LLM edge deployment.

entry.title: Learning When to Act: Interval-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Predictive Temporal Structure

author.name: Davide Di Gioia

entry.summary: Introduces interval-aware reinforcement learning where agents learn when to act using a hyperbolic geometry-based 'curvature signal' that measures uncertainty about future states, acting sooner when futures are divergent.

entry.title: Causal Discovery in Action: Learning Chain-Reaction Mechanisms from Interventions

author.name: Panayiotis Panayiotou, \"Ozg\"ur \c{S}im\c{s}ek

entry.summary: Studies causal discovery in chain-reaction systems where components activate sequentially, proving unique identifiability from blocking interventions and proposing an estimator with exponential error decay and logarithmic sample complexity.

entry.title: UniQueR: Unified Query-based Feedforward 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Chensheng Peng, Quentin Herau, Jiezhi Yang, Yichen Xie, Yihan Hu, Wenzhao Zheng, Matthew Strong, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: Presents UniQueR, a query-based feedforward 3D reconstruction framework from unposed images that formulates reconstruction as sparse 3D query inference, enabling prediction of occluded geometry in a single forward pass.

entry.title: Confidence Calibration under Ambiguous Ground Truth

author.name: Linwei Tao, Haoyang Luo, Minjing Dong, Chang Xu

entry.summary: Shows that standard confidence calibration methods fail when ground truth is ambiguous (annotators disagree), with Temperature Scaling systematically underestimating annotator uncertainty. Develops ambiguity-aware post-hoc calibrators using proper scoring rules.

entry.title: Set-Valued Prediction for Large Language Models with Feasibility-Aware Coverage Guarantees

author.name: Ye Li, Anqi Hu, Yuanchang Ye, Shiyan Tong, Zhiyuan Wang, Bo Fu

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for set-valued prediction from LLMs with feasibility-aware coverage guarantees, moving beyond single point predictions. Shows that valid answers may exist in the broader output space even when the top prediction is wrong.

entry.title: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Yutao Luo, Haotian Zhu, Shuchao Pang, Zhigang Lu, Tian Dong, Yongbin Zhou, Minhui Xue

entry.summary: Proposes AgentRAE, a backdoor attack against mobile GUI agents using visually natural triggers like app notification icons. Demonstrates that screenshot-based mobile agents have novel attack surfaces through notification-based visual backdoors.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Are Created Equal: Query-Efficient Jailbreak Fuzzing for LLMs

author.name: Wenyu Chen, Xiangtao Meng, Chuanchao Zang, Li Wang, Xinyu Gao, Jianing Wang, Peng Zhan, Zheng Li, Shanqing Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a query-efficient jailbreak fuzzing method that exploits the observation that token contributions to refusal are highly skewed, enabling targeted mutation of the most influential tokens rather than uniform mutation.

entry.title: Code Review Agent Benchmark

author.name: Yuntong Zhang, Zhiyuan Pan, Imam Nur Bani Yusuf, Haifeng Ruan, Ridwan Shariffdeen, Abhik Roychoudhury

entry.summary: Introduces c-CRAB, a code review benchmark for evaluating AI agents on pull request review tasks, addressing the quality assurance gap as AI-generated code proliferates.

entry.title: VTAM: Video-Tactile-Action Models for Complex Physical Interaction Beyond VLAs

author.name: Haoran Yuan, Weigang Yi, Zhenyu Zhang, Wendi Chen, Yuchen Mo, Jiashi Yin, Xinzhuo Li, Xiangyu Zeng, Chuan Wen, Cewu Lu, Katherine Driggs-Campbell, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: Introduces VTAM (Video-Tactile-Action Models), extending video-action models with tactile perception for contact-rich manipulation tasks where vision alone is insufficient for fine-grained force modulation.

entry.title: Failure of contextual invariance in gender inference with large language models

author.name: Sagar Kumar, Ariel Flint, Luca Maria Aiello, Andrea Baronchelli

entry.summary: Tests contextual invariance of LLMs in gender inference, finding that minimal, theoretically uninformative context causes large systematic shifts in model outputs and weakens correlations with cultural stereotypes.

entry.title: Implicit Turn-Wise Policy Optimization for Proactive User-LLM Interaction

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Yuxin Chen, Liang Luo, Buyun Zhang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Pan Li

entry.summary: Introduces ITPO (Implicit Turn-wise Policy Optimization) for multi-turn human-AI collaboration, using implicit process reward models to derive turn-wise rewards from sparse outcome signals for adaptive tutoring and recommendation.

entry.title: Latent Algorithmic Structure Precedes Grokking: A Mechanistic Study of ReLU MLPs on Modular Arithmetic

author.name: Anand Swaroop

entry.summary: Provides mechanistic analysis of grokking in ReLU MLPs on modular arithmetic, finding near-binary square wave input weights (not sinusoidal) and phase-sum relations in output weights. Shows algorithmic structure appears before the grokking transition.

entry.title: Optimal Variance-Dependent Regret Bounds for Infinite-Horizon MDPs

author.name: Guy Zamir, Matthew Zurek, Yudong Chen

entry.summary: Achieves the first optimal variance-dependent regret bounds for infinite-horizon MDPs (both average-reward and γ-regret), with a single tractable UCB-style algorithm that adapts to instance-specific complexity.

entry.title: Understanding the Challenges in Iterative Generative Optimization with LLMs

author.name: Allen Nie, Xavier Daull, Zhiyi Kuang, Abhinav Akkiraju, Anish Chaudhuri, Max Piasevoli, Ryan Rong, YuCheng Yuan, Prerit Choudhary, Shannon Xiao, Rasool Fakoor, Adith Swaminathan, Ching-An Cheng

entry.summary: Systematically investigates challenges in iterative LLM-based generative optimization, identifying hidden design choices (starting artifact, credit horizon, batching) that explain why self-improving agents are brittle in practice.

entry.title: Did You Forget What I Asked? Prospective Memory Failures in Large Language Models

author.name: Avni Mittal

entry.summary: Studies LLM formatting compliance failures through a cognitive psychology lens of 'prospective memory,' finding that compliance drops 2-21% under concurrent task load, with terminal constraints degrading up to 50%. Salience-enhanced prompting recovers much of the lost compliance.

entry.title: The Economics of Builder Saturation in Digital Markets

author.name: Armin Catovic

entry.summary: Formalizes the 'Builder Saturation Effect' where near-zero marginal production costs from generative AI lead to declining average returns per producer as finite human attention is diluted, resulting in increasing market concentration.

entry.title: Machine vision with small numbers of detected photons per inference

author.name: Shi-Yuan Ma, J\'er\'emie Laydevant, Mandar M. Sohoni, Logan G. Wright, Tianyu Wang, Peter L. McMahon

entry.summary: PANS (Photon-Aware Neuromorphic Sensing) enables machine vision with very few detected photons per inference through end-to-end optimization that incorporates photon statistics into training, achieving recognition in extremely photon-starved scenarios.

entry.title: Minimal Sufficient Representations for Self-interpretable Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Zhiyao Tan, Liu Li, Huazhen Lin

entry.summary: DeepIn is a self-interpretable neural network that adaptively identifies the minimal representation needed for full DNN expressivity, achieving optimal non-asymptotic error rates adapting to the learned minimal dimension.

entry.title: Leveraging Computerized Adaptive Testing for Cost-effective Evaluation of Large Language Models in Medical Benchmarking

author.name: Tianpeng Zheng, Zhehan Jiang, Jiayi Liu, Shicong Feng

entry.summary: Proposes a computerized adaptive testing framework based on item response theory for efficiently evaluating LLMs on medical knowledge, validating across 38 LLMs with a human-calibrated item bank.

entry.title: MedMT-Bench: Can LLMs Memorize and Understand Long Multi-Turn Conversations in Medical Scenarios?

author.name: Lin Yang, Yuancheng Yang, Xu Wang, Changkun Liu, Haihua Yang

entry.summary: MedMT-Bench is a medical multi-turn instruction following benchmark simulating entire diagnosis and treatment processes. It stress-tests long-context memory, interference robustness, and safety defense with 400 test cases averaging 22 rounds (up to 52). It fills a gap where existing medical benchmarks don't evaluate these practical requirements.

entry.title: Compression Method Matters: Benchmark-Dependent Output Dynamics in LLM Prompt Compression

author.name: Warren Johnson

entry.summary: This paper formalizes instruction survival probability (Psi) to explain benchmark-dependent output dynamics under prompt compression. Across 5,400 API calls, it shows strong benchmark effects where compression causes massive output expansion on some tasks (56x on MBPP) but not others, depending on whether critical prompt segments survive.

entry.title: Stance Labels Fail When They Matter Most: The Projection Problem in Stance Detection

author.name: Bowen Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies the 'projection problem' in stance detection where multi-dimensional attitudes are compressed into single Favor/Against/Neutral labels. When a text's dimensions conflict, annotator disagreement reflects different compression choices, not confusion. This creates systematic errors in politically charged texts.

entry.title: MARCH: Multi-Agent Reinforced Self-Check for LLM Hallucination

author.name: Zhuo Li, Yupeng Zhang, Pengyu Cheng, Jiajun Song, Mengyu Zhou, Hao Li, Shujie Hu, Yu Qin, Erchao Zhao, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: MARCH introduces a multi-agent framework for hallucination detection in RAG using deliberate information asymmetry between Solver, Proposer, and Checker agents. This addresses confirmation bias where a single verifier reproduces generation errors.

entry.title: LongTail Driving Scenarios with Reasoning Traces: The KITScenes LongTail Dataset

author.name: Royden Wagner, Omer Sahin Tas, Jaime Villa, Felix Hauser, Yinzhe Shen, Marlon Steiner, Dominik Strutz, Carlos Fernandez, Christian Kinzig, Guillermo S. Guitierrez-Cabello, Hendrik K\"onigshof, Fabian Immel, Richard Schwarzkopf, Nils Alexander Rack, Kevin R\"osch, Kaiwen Wang, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Martin Lauer, Igor Gilitschenski, Holger Caesar, Christoph Stiller

entry.summary: KITScenes LongTail is a dataset for end-to-end driving focusing on long-tail events with multi-view video, trajectories, instructions, and detailed reasoning traces. Includes multilingual reasoning traces from domain experts with diverse cultural backgrounds.

entry.title: See, Remember, Explore: A Benchmark and Baselines for Streaming Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Yuxi Wei, Wei Huang, Qirui Chen, Lu Hou, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: Introduces S3-Bench, a benchmark for streaming spatial question answering with active exploration, requiring temporally-grounded answers using only observations available up to query time, combining simulator and real-world settings.

entry.title: LensWalk: Agentic Video Understanding by Planning How You See in Videos

author.name: Keliang Li, Yansong Li, Hongze Shen, Mengdi Liu, Hong Chang, Shiguang Shan

entry.summary: Introduces LensWalk, an agentic video understanding framework where an LLM reasoner actively controls its own visual observation by dynamically specifying temporal scope and sampling density, creating a tight reason-plan-observe loop.

entry.title: TAG: Target-Agnostic Guidance for Stable Object-Centric Inference in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jiaying Zhou, Zhihao Zhan, Ruifeng Zhai, Qinhan Lyu, Hao Liu, Keze Wang, Liang Lin, Guangrun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TAG, an inference-time guidance mechanism for Vision-Language-Action models that reduces distractor-induced bias by contrasting predictions with and without the original observation, inspired by classifier-free guidance.

entry.title: ProGRank: Probe-Gradient Reranking to Defend Dense-Retriever RAG from Corpus Poisoning

author.name: Xiangyu Yin, Yi Qi, Chih-hong Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes ProGRank, a training-free retriever-side defense against corpus poisoning in dense-retriever RAG. Uses probe gradients from randomized perturbations to detect and rerank adversarial passages without auxiliary models.

entry.title: The Compression Paradox in LLM Inference: Provider-Dependent Energy Effects of Prompt Compression

author.name: Warren Johnson

entry.summary: This study tests whether prompt compression improves inference energy efficiency across 28,421 API trials with three providers, five benchmarks, and four compression ratios. It finds compression produced substantial quality loss while energy savings were provider-dependent, creating a 'compression paradox' for environmental sustainability claims.

entry.title: Session Risk Memory (SRM): Temporal Authorization for Deterministic Pre-Execution Safety Gates

author.name: Florin Adrian Chitan

entry.summary: Introduces Session Risk Memory (SRM), a lightweight module that extends stateless safety gates with trajectory-level authorization for AI agents, detecting distributed attacks that decompose harmful intent across multiple individually-compliant steps.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Generate Real-World Evidence? Evaluating Observational Studies in Medical Databases

author.name: Dubai Li, Yuxiang He, Yan Hu, Yu Tian, Jingsong Li

entry.summary: Introduces RWE-bench, a benchmark evaluating LLM agents' ability to conduct observational studies on MIMIC-IV database, generating tree-structured evidence bundles. Tests six LLMs on tasks derived from peer-reviewed studies.

entry.title: Between Rules and Reality: On the Context Sensitivity of LLM Moral Judgment

author.name: Adrian Sauter, Mona Schirmer

entry.summary: Evaluates context sensitivity of LLM moral judgments using Contextual MoralChoice dataset with systematic variations (consequentialist, emotional, relational). Finds that models and humans respond differently to contextual variations across 22 LLMs.

entry.title: RelayS2S: A Dual-Path Speculative Generation for Real-Time Dialogue

author.name: Long Mai

entry.summary: Presents RelayS2S, a hybrid architecture for real-time spoken dialogue that runs a fast duplex S2S path for low-latency response onset in parallel with a slower cascaded ASR→LLM path for higher-quality content, using speculative generation.

entry.title: UniFluids: Unified Neural Operator Learning with Conditional Flow-matching

author.name: Haosen Li, Qi Meng, Jiahao Li, Rui Zhang, Ruihua Song, Liang Ma, Zhi-Ming Ma

entry.summary: Presents UniFluids, a conditional flow-matching framework using diffusion Transformers to unify PDE solution operators across diverse PDEs with varying dimensionality. First flow-matching approach for unified operator learning with parallel generation.

entry.title: Causal Direct Preference Optimization for Distributionally Robust Generative Recommendation

author.name: Chu Zhao, Enneng Yang, Jianzhe Zhao, Guibing Guo

entry.summary: Proposes CausalDPO, extending Direct Preference Optimization with causal invariance learning to address spurious correlations amplified during alignment for LLM-based recommendation systems. Uses backdoor adjustment to improve out-of-distribution generalization.

entry.title: Reasoner-Executor-Synthesizer: Scalable Agentic Architecture with Static O(1) Context Window

author.name: Ivan Dobrovolskyi

entry.summary: Proposes Reasoner-Executor-Synthesizer (RES), a three-layer agentic architecture achieving O(1) token complexity by strictly separating intent parsing, deterministic data retrieval, and narrative generation, with the executor using zero LLM tokens.

entry.title: Learning to Trust: How Humans Mentally Recalibrate AI Confidence Signals

author.name: ZhaoBin Li, Mark Steyvers

entry.summary: Studies how humans learn to mentally recalibrate AI confidence signals through experience, finding robust learning across overconfidence, underconfidence, and even reverse-confidence conditions in a behavioral experiment with 200 participants.

entry.title: KARMA: Knowledge-Action Regularized Multimodal Alignment for Personalized Search at Taobao

author.name: Zhi Sun, Wenming Zhang, Yi Wei, Liren Yu, Zhixuan Zhang, Dan Ou, Haihong Tang

entry.summary: Introduces KARMA for personalized search at Taobao, identifying a 'Knowledge-Action Gap' when fine-tuning LLMs for personalization, where action-only training causes semantic collapse. Proposes knowledge-action regularization to preserve pre-trained knowledge.

entry.title: ForestPrune: High-ratio Visual Token Compression for Video Multimodal Large Language Models via Spatial-Temporal Forest Modeling

author.name: Shaobo Ju, Baiyang Song, Tao Chen, Jiapeng Zhang, Qiong Wu, Chao Chang, HuaiXi Wang, Yiyi Zhou, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: Proposes ForestPrune, a training-free token pruning method for video MLLMs that constructs spatial-temporal token forests across video frames for high-ratio compression. Achieves significant token reduction while maintaining video understanding quality.

entry.title: Why AI-Generated Text Detection Fails: Evidence from Explainable AI Beyond Benchmark Accuracy

author.name: Shushanta Pudasaini, Luis Miralles-Pechu\'an, David Lillis, Marisa Llorens Salvador

entry.summary: Investigates whether AI-generated text detectors genuinely identify machine authorship or merely exploit dataset artifacts. Shows through explainable AI that high benchmark accuracy can mask reliance on spurious features.

entry.title: Emergence of Fragility in LLM-based Social Networks: the Case of Moltbook

author.name: Luca Sodano, Sofia Sciangula, Amulya Galmarini, Francesco Bertolotti

entry.summary: Analyzes the interaction network of Moltbook, a social platform composed entirely of LLM-based agents, revealing strongly heterogeneous connectivity patterns and fragility in the emergent social network structure.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Introducing a Symbolic-Mechanistic Approach to Interpretable Evaluation

author.name: Reza Habibi, Darian Lee, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: Argues for mechanism-aware evaluation combining symbolic rules with mechanistic interpretability, demonstrating on NL-to-SQL that a memorization model achieves 94% accuracy on standard benchmarks despite lacking genuine understanding.

entry.title: A Theory of LLM Information Susceptibility

author.name: Zhuo-Yang Song, Hua Xing Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a theoretical framework for 'LLM information susceptibility' - characterizing fundamental limits on how much a fixed LLM can improve strategy performance as computational resources scale. Develops a multi-variable utility framework with empirical validation.

entry.title: Can VLMs Reason Robustly? A Neuro-Symbolic Investigation

author.name: Weixin Chen, Antonio Vergari, Han Zhao

entry.summary: Studies whether VLMs can reason robustly under covariate shifts in visual deductive reasoning tasks. Finds that fine-tuned VLMs fail under distribution shifts and proposes a neuro-symbolic pipeline combining VLM perception with symbolic reasoning for robust generalization.

entry.title: MoE-Sieve: Routing-Guided LoRA for Efficient MoE Fine-Tuning

author.name: Andrea Manzoni

entry.summary: Proposes MoE-Sieve, which profiles expert routing distributions and applies LoRA only to the most frequently activated experts per layer, finding that tuning just 25% of experts maintains competitive performance.

entry.title: LLM Inference at the Edge: Mobile, NPU, and GPU Performance Efficiency Trade-offs Under Sustained Load

author.name: Pranay Tummalapalli, Sahil Arayakandy, Ritam Pal, Kautuk Kundan

entry.summary: Benchmarks Qwen 2.5 1.5B (4-bit quantized) across four platforms (Raspberry Pi with NPU, Samsung Galaxy, iPhone, laptop GPU) and finds that thermal management supersedes peak compute as the primary constraint for sustained on-device LLM inference.

entry.title: Beyond Consistency: Inference for the Relative risk functional in Deep Nonparametric Cox Models

author.name: Sattwik Ghosal, Xuran Meng, Yi Li

entry.summary: Develops asymptotic distribution theory for deep Cox proportional hazards estimators, linking optimization error to population risk and enabling valid inference with uncertainty quantification for survival analysis.

entry.title: Attention-aware Inference Optimizations for Large Vision-Language Models with Memory-efficient Decoding

author.name: Fatih Ilhan, Gaowen Liu, Ramana Rao Kompella, Selim Furkan Tekin, Tiansheng Huang, Zachary Yahn, Yichang Xu, Ling Liu

entry.summary: AttentionPack is an adaptive attention-aware optimization framework for vision-language model inference that improves memory efficiency during decoding for long-context tasks with high-resolution images or videos.

entry.title: Visuospatial Perspective Taking in Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Jonathan Prunty, Seraphina Zhang, Patrick Quinn, Jianxun Lian, Xing Xie, Lucy Cheke

entry.summary: Evaluates multimodal language models on visuospatial perspective-taking tasks adapted from human cognitive studies, finding pronounced deficits in Level 2 VPT (adopting another's viewpoint) requiring self-perspective inhibition.

entry.title: Berta: an open-source, modular tool for AI-enabled clinical documentation

author.name: Samridhi Vaid, Mike Weldon, Jesse Dunn, Sacha Davis, Kevin Lonergan, Henry Li, Jeffrey Franc, Mohamed Abdalla, Daniel C. Baumgart, Jake Hayward, J Ross Mitchell

entry.summary: Berta is an open-source modular AI scribe platform for clinical documentation deployed at Alberta Health Services. Over 8 months, 198 emergency physicians used it across 105 facilities, keeping all data within secure institutional infrastructure. It addresses the cost and data governance concerns of commercial AI scribes ($99-600/physician/month).

entry.title: Cluster-R1: Large Reasoning Models Are Instruction-following Clustering Agents

author.name: Peijun Qing, Puneet Mathur, Nedim Lipka, Varun Manjunatha, Ryan Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt, Saeed Hassanpour, Soroush Vosoughi

entry.summary: Cluster-R1 reframes instruction-following text clustering as a generative task using large reasoning models as autonomous clustering agents. It enables models to interpret high-level clustering instructions and infer latent groupings, including determining optimal cluster counts. The ReasonCluster benchmark is introduced for evaluation.

entry.title: Improving Lean4 Autoformalization via Cycle Consistency Fine-tuning

author.name: Arsen Shebzukhov

entry.summary: Fine-tunes Qwen3.5-2B for Lean4 autoformalization using cycle consistency reward with GRPO, where consistency is measured through a NL→Lean4→NL' round-trip. Compares with supervised fine-tuning with and without curriculum learning on FineLeanCorpus.

entry.title: OneSearch-V2: The Latent Reasoning Enhanced Self-distillation Generative Search Framework

author.name: Ben Chen, Siyuan Wang, Yufei Ma, Zihan Liang, Xuxin Zhang, Yue Lv, Ying Yang, Huangyu Dai, Lingtao Mao, Tong Zhao, Zhipeng Qian, Xinyu Sun, Zhixin Zhai, Yang Zhao, Bochao Liu, Jingshan Lv, Xiao Liang, Hui Kong, Jing Chen, Han Li, Chenyi Lei, Wenwu Ou, Kun Gai

entry.summary: OneSearch-V2 is a latent reasoning enhanced self-distillation generative search framework for industrial-scale deployment. Addresses complex query understanding, latent user intent exploitation, and overfitting to narrow historical preferences in generative retrieval.

entry.title: M3T: Discrete Multi-Modal Motion Tokens for Sign Language Production

author.name: Alexandre Symeonidis-Herzig, Jianhe Low, Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Richard Bowden

entry.summary: M3T proposes SMPL-FX (coupling FLAME with SMPL-X) and modality-specific Finite Scalar Quantization VAEs for sign language production with non-manual features. Addresses the barrier that standard body models lack sufficient facial expressiveness for grammatically obligatory non-manual features.

entry.title: AdvSplat: Adversarial Attacks on Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting Models

author.name: Yiran Qiao, Yiren Lu, Yunlai Zhou, Rui Yang, Linlin Hou, Yu Yin, Jing Ma

entry.summary: First systematic study of adversarial attacks on feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting models, introducing AdvSplat. Demonstrates both white-box and transferable attacks on neural-network-backed 3DGS systems increasingly considered for commercial deployment.

entry.title: GenMask: Adapting DiT for Segmentation via Direct Mask

author.name: Yuhuan Yang, Xianwei Zhuang, Yuxuan Cai, Chaofan Ma, Shuai Bai, Jiangchao Yao, Ya Zhang, Junyang Lin, Yanfeng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces GenMask, which adapts Diffusion Transformers (DiT) for segmentation by directly generating masks in a generative manner, identifying that VAE latents of binary masks have distinct properties from natural images and proposing timestep sampling strategies.

entry.title: DP^2-VL: Private Photo Dataset Protection by Data Poisoning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hongyi Miao, Jun Jia, Xincheng Wang, Qianli Ma, Wei Sun, Wangqiu Zhou, Dandan Zhu, Yewen Cao, Zhi Liu, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: Proposes DP²-VL for protecting private photo datasets from VLM-based identity-affiliation learning attacks, where attackers fine-tune VLMs to link facial identities with private information. Introduces data poisoning defense.

entry.title: Mitigating Object Hallucinations in LVLMs via Attention Imbalance Rectification

author.name: Han Sun, Qin Li, Peixin Wang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies attention imbalance across modalities and tokens as a causal factor for object hallucination in LVLMs, proposing attention imbalance rectification as a mitigation strategy.

entry.title: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare

author.name: Akash Ghosh, Tajamul Ashraf, Rishu Kumar Singh, Numan Saeed, Sriparna Saha, Xiuying Chen, Salman Khan

entry.summary: Introduces CareFlow benchmark and CarePilot multi-agent framework for long-horizon computer task automation in healthcare, targeting medical annotation tools, DICOM viewers, EHR systems, etc.

entry.title: ScrollScape: Unlocking 32K Image Generation With Video Diffusion Priors

author.name: Haodong Yu, Yabo Zhang, Donglin Di, Ruyi Zhang, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: Presents ScrollScape, which reformulates extreme-aspect-ratio image generation as continuous video generation, leveraging video diffusion priors to synthesize ultra-high-resolution images up to 32K without object repetition.

entry.title: Toward Physically Consistent Driving Video World Models under Challenging Trajectories

author.name: Jiawei Zhou, Zhenxin Zhu, Lingyi Du, Linye Lyu, Lijun Zhou, Zhanqian Wu, Hongcheng Luo, Zhuotao Tian, Bing Wang, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Haiyang Sun, Yu Li

entry.summary: Proposes PhyGenesis, a world model for generating physically consistent driving videos even under challenging or counterfactual trajectories, addressing the failure of existing models when conditioned on non-naturalistic driving scenarios.

entry.title: Learning Actionable Manipulation Recovery via Counterfactual Failure Synthesis

author.name: Dayou Li, Jiuzhou Lei, Hao Wang, Lulin Liu, Yunhao Yang, Zihan Wang, Bangya Liu, Minghui Zheng, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: Introduces Dream2Fix, a framework that synthesizes photorealistic counterfactual failure rollouts from successful demonstrations for learning robotic manipulation recovery, bridging the gap between failure diagnosis and actionable recovery.

entry.title: Chameleon: Episodic Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Xinying Guo, Chenxi Jiang, Hyun Bin Kim, Ying Sun, Yang Xiao, Yuhang Han, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Chameleon, an episodic memory system for long-horizon robotic manipulation that preserves fine-grained perceptual cues through geometry-grounded multimodal tokens and goal-directed recall via a differentiable memory stack.

entry.title: SafeFlow: Real-Time Text-Driven Humanoid Whole-Body Control via Physics-Guided Rectified Flow and Selective Safety Gating

author.name: Hanbyel Cho, Sang-Hun Kim, Jeonguk Kang, Donghan Koo

entry.summary: Proposes SafeFlow, a text-driven humanoid whole-body control framework combining physics-guided rectified flow motion generation with a 3-stage safety gate to prevent physically infeasible motions, especially under out-of-distribution inputs.

entry.title: Elements of Conformal Prediction for Statisticians

author.name: Matteo Sesia, Stefano Favaro

entry.summary: Provides a comprehensive exposition of conformal prediction for statisticians, covering the distribution-free, model-agnostic framework that provides finite-sample coverage guarantees for predictive inference.

entry.title: $1 billion is not enough; OpenAI Foundation must start spending tens of billions each year

author.name: Davidmanheim

entry.summary: Argues that OpenAI Foundation's commitment to spend 'at least $1 billion' over the coming year is vastly insufficient given its $150B+ equity stake and OpenAI's stated mission to benefit humanity. Calls for tens of billions in annual spending. Critiques the nonprofit restructuring as inadequate.

entry.title: ABSTRAL: Automatic Design of Multi-Agent Systems Through Iterative Refinement and Topology Optimization

author.name: Weijia Song, Jiashu Yue, Zhe Pang

entry.summary: Introduces ABSTRAL, treating multi-agent system architecture as an evolving natural-language document refined through contrastive trace analysis. Measures 'multi-agent coordination tax' showing 26% turn efficiency with 66% task exhaustion rates, while demonstrating transferable design knowledge.

entry.title: Empirical Comparison of Agent Communication Protocols for Task Orchestration

author.name: Ivan Dobrovolskyi

entry.summary: Presents the first empirical comparison of tool-integration-only, multi-agent delegation, and hybrid architectures across three complexity tiers. Addresses the gap between industry adoption and academic understanding of agent communication protocols.

entry.title: Describe-Then-Act: Proactive Agent Steering via Distilled Language-Action World Models

author.name: Massimiliano Pappa, Luca Romani, Valentino Sacco, Alessio Palma, St\'ephane Lathuili\`ere, Fabio Galasso, Xavier Alameda-Pineda, Indro Spinelli

entry.summary: Introduces DILLO, a fast steering layer for safety-critical agents that predicts action outcomes from latent states rather than visual simulation, shifting from 'simulate-then-act' to 'describe-then-act' for proactive agent safety.

entry.title: Founder effects shape the evolutionary dynamics of multimodality in open LLM families

author.name: Manuel Cebrian

entry.summary: Analyzes how multimodal capabilities propagate within open LLM families using Hugging Face metadata (>1.8M models). Finds multimodality remains rare through 2023-2024 then increases sharply, dominated by image-text tasks, with 'founder effects' shaping capability evolution.

entry.title: Sample Transform Cost-Based Training-Free Hallucination Detector for Large Language Models

author.name: Zeyang Ding, Xinglin Hu, Jicong Fan

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free hallucination detector using optimal transport distances between token embeddings of pairwise LLM responses. Argues distribution complexity indicates hallucination and avoids the challenge of unknown density estimation.

entry.title: When Visuals Aren't the Problem: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Misleading Data Visualizations

author.name: Harsh Nishant Lalai, Raj Sanjay Shah, Hanspeter Pfister, Sashank Varma, Grace Guo

entry.summary: Evaluates vision-language models on detecting misleading visualizations using a fine-grained taxonomy of reasoning errors and visualization design errors, finding VLMs struggle more with subtle reasoning errors in captions than visual design flaws.

entry.title: Rethinking Multimodal Fusion for Time Series: Auxiliary Modalities Need Constrained Fusion

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Jaehoon Lee, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, SoonYoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: Shows that naive multimodal fusion (addition/concatenation) of auxiliary modalities into time series forecasting often hurts performance, and proposes constrained fusion methods that control auxiliary information integration to consistently improve results.

entry.title: Stability-Preserving Online Adaptation of Neural Closed-loop Maps

author.name: Danilo Saccani, Luca Furieri, Giancarlo Ferrari-Trecate

entry.summary: Introduces a stability-preserving update mechanism for online adaptation of neural network controllers, proving that switching between stabilizing policies can itself destabilize systems and providing gain-based conditions for safe updates.

entry.title: Vision-based Deep Learning Analysis of Unordered Biomedical Tabular Datasets via Optimal Spatial Cartography

author.name: Sakib Mostafa, Tarik Massoud, Maximilian Diehn, Lei Xing, Md Tauhidul Islam

entry.summary: Introduces Dynomap, an end-to-end framework that learns task-optimized spatial arrangements of tabular features for processing with vision architectures, enabling CNNs/ViTs to exploit local structure in inherently non-spatial biomedical data.

entry.title: PhotoAgent: A Robotic Photographer with Spatial and Aesthetic Understanding

author.name: Lirong Che, Zhenfeng Gan, Yanbo Chen, Junbo Tan, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PhotoAgent, a robotic photographer that translates aesthetic goals into geometric constraints via LMM reasoning, then iteratively refines viewpoints through mental simulation in a 3DGS-based internal world model.

entry.title: Assessing the Robustness of Climate Foundation Models under No-Analog Distribution Shifts

author.name: Maria Conchita Agana Navarro, Geng Li, Theo Wolf, Maria Perez-Ortiz

entry.summary: Assesses robustness of ML-based climate emulators under 'no-analog' distribution shifts where future climate states fall outside historical training data. Addresses the critical challenge of data contamination in evaluation.

entry.title: 3DCity-LLM: Empowering Multi-modality Large Language Models for 3D City-scale Perception and Understanding

author.name: Yiping Chen, Jinpeng Li, Wenyu Ke, Yang Luo, Jie Ouyang, Zhongjie He, Li Liu, Hongchao Fan, Hao Wu

entry.summary: Proposes 3DCity-LLM, a framework for 3D city-scale vision-language understanding with a coarse-to-fine encoding strategy and a 1.2M sample dataset across seven task categories for urban scene understanding.

entry.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning with Preference-based Constraint Inference

author.name: Chenglin Li, Guangchun Ruan, Hua Geng

entry.summary: Proposes preference-based constraint inference for safe RL, identifying that Bradley-Terry models fail to capture asymmetric, heavy-tailed safety costs, leading to risk underestimation.

entry.title: The Geometric Price of Discrete Logic: Context-driven Manifold Dynamics of Number Representations

author.name: Long Zhang, Dai-jun Lin, Wei-neng Chen

entry.summary: Reveals how LLMs form discrete decision boundaries for logical reasoning through 'topological distortion' driven by task context, using Gram-Schmidt decomposition of residual-stream activations.

entry.title: Deep Neural Regression Collapse

author.name: Akshay Rangamani, Altay Unal

entry.summary: Establishes that Neural Regression Collapse occurs in deeper layers (not just the last), showing features lie in a target-dimension subspace with aligned covariance. Extends neural collapse theory from classification to regression across multiple architectures.

entry.title: Can we generate portable representations for clinical time series data using LLMs?

author.name: Zongliang Ji, Yifei Sun, Andre Amaral, Anna Goldenberg, Rahul G. Krishnan

entry.summary: Studies whether frozen LLMs can create portable patient embeddings from ICU time series by converting irregular data to natural language summaries, enabling cross-hospital model transfer with minimal retraining.

entry.title: Marchuk: Efficient Global Weather Forecasting from Mid-Range to Sub-Seasonal Scales via Flow Matching

author.name: Arsen Kuzhamuratov, Mikhail Zhirnov, Andrey Kuznetsov, Ivan Oseledets, Konstantin Sobolev

entry.summary: Presents Marchuk, a generative latent flow-matching model for global weather forecasting from mid-range to subseasonal timescales (up to 30 days), using trainable positional embeddings and extended temporal context.

entry.title: DepthCharge: A Domain-Agnostic Framework for Measuring Depth-Dependent Knowledge in Large Language Models

author.name: Alexander Sheppert

entry.summary: DepthCharge is a framework for measuring how deeply LLMs can sustain accurate responses under adaptive follow-up questioning across arbitrary domains, using adaptive probing, on-demand fact verification, and survival statistics.

entry.title: Dual-Gated Epistemic Time-Dilation: Autonomous Compute Modulation in Asynchronous MARL

author.name: Igor Jankowski

entry.summary: ETD-MAPPO enables multi-agent RL agents to autonomously modulate their execution frequency based on epistemic uncertainty, replacing fixed synchronous execution with adaptive compute allocation for edge deployment.

entry.title: Knowledge-Guided Manipulation Using Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Aditya Narendra, Mukhammadrizo Maribjonov, Dmitry Makarov, Dmitry Yudin, Aleksandr Panov

entry.summary: KG-M3PO combines knowledge graphs with multi-task model-based RL for robotic manipulation, using online 3D scene graphs with dynamic spatial/affordance edges trained end-to-end through the RL objective.

entry.title: DVM: Real-Time Kernel Generation for Dynamic AI Models

author.name: Jingzhi Fang, Xiong Gao, Renwei Zhang, Zichun Ye, Lei Chen, Jie Zhao, Chengnuo Huang, Hui Xu, Xuefeng Jin

entry.summary: DVM is a real-time compiler for dynamic AI models that uses a bytecode virtual machine to speed up runtime compilation, addressing the latency caused by dynamic tensor shapes and control flows.

entry.title: Federated fairness-aware classification under differential privacy

author.name: Gengyu Xue, Yi Yu

entry.summary: FDP-Fair is a two-step algorithm for fairness-aware classification under federated differential privacy, with a lightweight single-server variant CDP-Fair, providing theoretical guarantees under mild structural assumptions.

entry.title: Retrieval Improvements Do Not Guarantee Better Answers: A Study of RAG for AI Policy QA

author.name: Saahil Mathur, Ryan David Rittner, Vedant Ajit Thakur, Daniel Stuart Schiff, Tunazzina Islam

entry.summary: Studies RAG for AI policy analysis using a curated corpus of 947 AI policy documents, finding that retrieval improvements from fine-tuning don't necessarily translate to better generated answers.

entry.title: Training a Large Language Model for Medical Coding Using Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Clinical Data

author.name: John Cook, Michael Wyatt, Peng Wei, Iris Chin, Santosh Gupta, Van Zyl Van Vuuren, Richie Siburian, Amanda Spicer, Kristen Viviano, Alda Cami, Raunaq Malhotra, Zhewei Yao, Jeff Rasley, Gaurav Kaushik

entry.summary: This paper investigates fine-tuning an open-weight LLM for ICD-10-CM and CPT medical coding using privacy-preserving synthetic clinical data. It addresses the challenge of heterogeneous records and long-tail code distributions without exposing real patient data. The approach demonstrates that synthetic data can bridge the gap for expert-level medical coding tasks.

entry.title: Navigating the Concept Space of Language Models

author.name: Wilson E. Marc\'ilio-Jr, Danilo M. Eler

entry.summary: Concept Explorer is an interactive system for post-hoc exploration of Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) features from LLMs, organizing concept explanations using hierarchical neighborhood embeddings. It enables multi-resolution navigation from coarse concept clusters to individual features, addressing the difficulty of exploring thousands of SAE features at scale.

entry.title: From Oracle to Noisy Context: Mitigating Contextual Exposure Bias in Speech-LLMs

author.name: Xiaoyong Guo, Nanjie Li, Zijie Zeng, Kai Wang, Hao Huang, Haihua Xu, Wei Shi

entry.summary: Addresses contextual exposure bias in Speech-LLMs where training uses oracle conversation history but inference uses error-prone history. Proposes Teacher Error Knowledge, Context Dropout, and DPO to improve robustness, showing consistent gains on TED-LIUM 3 and LibriSpeech.

entry.title: GameplayQA: A Benchmarking Framework for Decision-Dense POV-Synced Multi-Video Understanding of 3D Virtual Agents

author.name: Yunzhe Wang, Runhui Xu, Kexin Zheng, Tianyi Zhang, Jayavibhav Niranjan Kogundi, Soham Hans, Volkan Ustun

entry.summary: GameplayQA benchmarks agentic-centric perception and reasoning through densely annotated multiplayer 3D gameplay videos at 1.22 labels/second. Evaluates multi-agent behaviors from first-person perspective with time-synced captions structured around Self, Other Agents, and World.

entry.title: Mechanic: Sorrifier-Driven Formal Decomposition Workflow for Automated Theorem Proving

author.name: Ruichen Qiu, Yichuan Cao, Junqi Liu, Dakai Guo, Xiao-Shan Gao, Lihong Zhi, Ruyong Feng

entry.summary: Mechanic proposes a 'Sorrifier-Driven' formal decomposition workflow for automated theorem proving, addressing the challenge of handling failed proof attempts without discarding correct partial progress or accumulating excessive context.

entry.title: LLMs Do Not Grade Essays Like Humans

author.name: Jerin George Mathew, Sumayya Taher, Anindita Kundu, Denilson Barbosa

entry.summary: Shows that LLM-generated essay scores have weak agreement with human grades and vary with essay characteristics. LLMs tend to give higher scores to short/underdeveloped essays and lower scores to longer essays with minor errors. LLM scores are more compressed than human ratings.

entry.title: FilterGS: Traversal-Free Parallel Filtering and Adaptive Shrinking for Large-Scale LoD 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yixian Wang, Haolin Yu, Jiadong Tang, Yu Gao, Xihan Wang, Yufeng Yue, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Introduces FilterGS, a parallel filtering mechanism for large-scale Level-of-Detail 3D Gaussian Splatting that eliminates serial tree traversal (>60% of render time) and reduces redundant Gaussian-tile pairs via a novel GTC metric.

entry.title: Revealing Multi-View Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Wooje Park, Insu Lee, Soohyun Kim, Jaeyun Jang, Minyoung Noh, Kyuhong Shim, Byonghyo Shim

entry.summary: Identifies and benchmarks 'multi-view hallucination' in LVLMs, where models confuse visual information across different viewpoints or instances, proposing Reference Shift Contrastive Decoding (RSCD) as a training-free mitigation.

entry.title: PointRFT: Explicit Reinforcement Fine-tuning for Point Cloud Few-shot Learning

author.name: Yankai Wang, Yiding Sun, Qirui Wang, Pengbo Li, Chaoyi Lu, Dongxu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes PointRFT, the first reinforcement fine-tuning paradigm for point cloud learning using GRPO-style reward optimization, applying RL-based training to 3D foundation models for few-shot classification.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Priors: Mitigating Optimization Collapse for Generalizable Visual Forensics

author.name: Jipeng Liu, Haichao Shi, Siyu Xing, Rong Yin, Xiao-Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies 'Optimization Collapse' in CLIP-based deepfake detectors trained with SAM, where performance degrades to random guessing, and proposes Critical Optimization Radius theory with GSNR-based analysis.

entry.title: AD-Reasoning: Multimodal Guideline-Guided Reasoning for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Qiuhui Chen, Yushan Deng, Xuancheng Yao, Yi Hong

entry.summary: Presents AD-Reasoning, a multimodal framework for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis that integrates structural MRI with clinical data and uses reinforcement fine-tuning with rule-based verifiers for NIA-AA guideline-consistent diagnoses.

entry.title: RVLM: Recursive Vision-Language Models with Adaptive Depth

author.name: Nicanor Mayumu, Zeenath Khan, Melodena Stephens, Patrick Mukala, Farhad Oroumchian

entry.summary: Proposes RVLM, a recursive vision-language model for medical AI that uses iterative generate-execute loops with Python code and vision sub-agents, providing auditable reasoning chains with adaptive iteration depth.

entry.title: TopoMesh: High-Fidelity Mesh Autoencoding via Topological Unification

author.name: Guan Luo, Xiu Li, Rui Chen, Xuanyu Yi, Jing Lin, Chia-Hao Chen, Jiahang Liu, Song-Hai Zhang, Jianfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TopoMesh, a mesh VAE that addresses topology mismatch between GT meshes and network predictions by establishing explicit mesh-level correspondences through topological unification, preserving sharp features.

entry.title: Causal Transfer in Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Mohammed M. Abdelsamea, Daniel Tweneboah Anyimadu, Tasneem Selim, Saif Alzubi, Lei Zhang, Ahmed Karam Eldaly, Xujiong Ye

entry.summary: A survey paper that systematizes Causal Transfer Learning (CTL) for medical image analysis, framing domain shift as a causal problem and analyzing how causal reasoning can enable more robust clinical AI across hospitals and imaging protocols.

entry.title: CAPTCHA Solving for Native GUI Agents: Automated Reasoning-Action Data Generation and Self-Corrective Training

author.name: Yuxi Chen, Haoyu Zhai, Chenkai Wang, Rui Yang, Lingming Zhang, Gang Wang, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces ReCAP, a CAPTCHA-capable native GUI agent that can solve interactive CAPTCHAs using VLMs while preserving general GUI agent capabilities, with a self-corrective training pipeline and dynamic CAPTCHA benchmark.

entry.title: Event-Driven Proactive Assistive Manipulation with Grounded Vision-Language Planning

author.name: Fengkai Liu, Hao Su, Haozhuang Chi, Rui Geng, Congzhi Ren, Xuqing Liu, Yucheng Xu, Yuichi Ohsita, Liyun Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces an event-driven proactive robotic assistance framework where robots infer the next helpful action from observed workspace state transitions rather than waiting for user instructions, using vision-language planning.

entry.title: PCHC: Enabling Preference Conditioned Humanoid Control via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Huanyu Li, Dewei Wang, Xinmiao Wang, Xinzhe Liu, Peng Liu, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Proposes PCHC, a multi-objective RL framework enabling a single preference-conditioned policy to balance competing objectives for humanoid control (e.g., speed vs energy), rather than training separate policies.

entry.title: SOMA: Strategic Orchestration and Memory-Augmented System for Vision-Language-Action Model Robustness via In-Context Adaptation

author.name: Zhuoran Li, Zhiyang Li, Kaijun Zhou, Jinyu Gu

entry.summary: Proposes SOMA, a memory-augmented system for improving VLA model robustness through contrastive dual-memory RAG, LLM-based failure attribution, and MCP interventions, all without fine-tuning the frozen VLA policy.

entry.title: 3D-Mix for VLA: A Plug-and-Play Module for Integrating VGGT-based 3D Information into Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Xiaopeng Lin, Zhaolong Shen, Yuliang Wei, Haishan Liu, Changti Wu, Hang Yuan, Bailing Wang, Cong Huang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic comparison of nine VGGT integration schemes for adding 3D spatial information to VLA models, finding that semantic-conditioned gated fusion optimally balances 2D and 3D features for manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Reflected diffusion models adapt to low-dimensional data

author.name: Asbj{\o}rn Holk, Claudia Strauch, Lukas Trottner

entry.summary: Provides statistical analysis showing reflected diffusion models on bounded domains adapt to low-dimensional data structure, developing analytic tools for score approximation by sparse ReLU networks on the hypercube.

entry.title: Learning What Matters Now: Dynamic Preference Inference under Contextual Shifts

author.name: Xianwei Cao, Dou Quan, Zhenliang Zhang, Shuang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Dynamic Preference Inference (DPI) for sequential decision-making where preference weights are unobserved latent variables that drift with context. Uses variational inference to maintain probabilistic beliefs over preferences, inspired by cognitive science.

entry.title: Optimizing Small Language Models for NL2SQL via Chain-of-Thought Fine-Tuning

author.name: Anshul Solanki, Sanchit Latawa, Koushik Chakraborty, Navneet Kamboj

entry.summary: Shows a counter-intuitive finding that fine-tuning large models (Gemini 2.5 Flash/Lite) on NL2SQL yields negligible returns while small models (Qwen) show significant gains. Chain-of-thought fine-tuning improved small model performance from 36% to 45%.

entry.title: MedCausalX: Adaptive Causal Reasoning with Self-Reflection for Trustworthy Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jianxin Lin, Chunzheng Zhu, Peter J. Kneuertz, Yunfei Bai, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: Proposes MedCausalX, an end-to-end framework for causal reasoning in medical VLMs with adaptive causal correction, causal-spurious contrastive samples, and causal consistency across reasoning trajectories. Introduces CRMed dataset.

entry.title: Latent Semantic Manifolds in Large Language Models

author.name: Mohamed A. Mabrok

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical framework interpreting LLM hidden states as points on a Riemannian submanifold with Fisher information metric. Defines the 'expressibility gap' measuring semantic distortion from vocabulary discretization and proves rate-distortion bounds.

entry.title: Instruction-Tuned, but Not More Verifiable Instruction-Following: A Cross-Task Diagnosis for LoRA Adapters

author.name: Junyi Zou

entry.summary: Examines whether LoRA adapter labels (e.g., 'instruction-tuned') reliably predict actual capability improvements, finding nominal labels often fail to predict performance on verifiable instruction-following tasks (IFEval) with clear configuration sensitivity.

entry.title: Color When It Counts: Grayscale-Guided Online Triggering for Always-On Streaming Video Sensing

author.name: Weitong Cai, Hang Zhang, Yukai Huang, Shitong Sun, Jiankang Deng, Songcen Xu, Jifei Song, Zhensong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes ColorTrigger, a grayscale-always, color-on-demand paradigm for edge video sensing that selectively activates RGB capture based on grayscale affinity analysis, enabling efficient always-on video understanding for resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: LGSE: Lexically Grounded Subword Embedding Initialization for Low-Resource Language Adaptation

author.name: Hailay Teklehaymanot, Dren Fazlija, Wolfgang Nejdl

entry.summary: Proposes LGSE, a framework for adapting pretrained models to low-resource morphologically rich languages by using morphologically informed segmentation for embedding initialization of novel tokens, rather than arbitrary subword units.

entry.title: Focus, Don't Prune: Identifying Instruction-Relevant Regions for Information-Rich Image Understanding

author.name: Mincheol Kwon, Minseung Lee, Seonga Choi, Miso Choi, Kyeong-Jin Oh, Hyunyoung Lee, Cheonyoung Park, Yongho Song, Seunghyun Park, Jinkyu Kim

entry.summary: Proposes PinPoint, a two-stage framework for LVLMs that first identifies instruction-relevant image regions then extracts fine-grained features, reducing visual token overhead for information-rich images like infographics and documents.

entry.title: Off-Policy Evaluation and Learning for Survival Outcomes under Censoring

author.name: Kohsuke Kubota, Mitsuhiro Takahashi, Yuta Saito

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for off-policy evaluation and learning tailored to survival outcomes with right-censored data, introducing IPCW-IPS estimators. Addresses the systematic bias in standard OPE estimators that ignore censoring.

entry.title: Curriculum-Driven 3D CT Report Generation via Language-Free Visual Grafting and Zone-Constrained Compression

author.name: V. K. Cody Bumgardner, Mitchell A. Klusty, Mahmut S. Gokmen, Evan W. Damron

entry.summary: Presents Ker-VLJEPA-3B, a four-phase curriculum learning framework for generating radiology reports from 3D CT volumes, using a self-supervised visual backbone trained without text supervision.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM-Based Test Generation Under Software Evolution

author.name: Sabaat Haroon, Mohammad Taha Khan, Muhammad Ali Gulzar

entry.summary: Large-scale empirical study of LLM-based test generation under program evolution, analyzing how generated tests respond to semantic-altering vs semantic-preserving code changes across multiple LLMs.

entry.title: StateLinFormer: Stateful Training Enhancing Long-term Memory in Navigation

author.name: Zhiyuan Chen, Yuxuan Zhong, Fan Wang, Bo Yu, Pengtao Shao, Shaoshan Liu, Ning Ding

entry.summary: Introduces StateLinFormer, a linear-attention navigation model with stateful memory that preserves recurrent states across training segments, approximating learning on infinitely long sequences for long-horizon navigation.

entry.title: An Invariant Compiler for Neural ODEs in AI-Accelerated Scientific Simulation

author.name: Fangzhou Yu, Yiqi Su, Ray Lee, Shenfeng Cheng, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: Presents an invariant compiler that treats physical conservation laws as first-class types and uses an LLM-driven compilation workflow to enforce hard constraints on neural ODE trajectories for scientific simulation.

entry.title: Towards Effective Experiential Learning: Dual Guidance for Utilization and Internalization

author.name: Fei Bai, Zhipeng Chen, Chuan Hao, Ming Yang, Ran Tao, Bryan Dai, Wayne Xin Zhao, Jian Yang, Hongteng Xu

entry.summary: Proposes DGO (Dual Guidance Optimization), a framework for RLVR training of LLMs that leverages both external experience (retrieved solutions) and internal experience (self-generated trajectories) to guide exploration and knowledge internalization.

entry.title: MolEvolve: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search for Interpretable Molecular Optimization

author.name: Xiangsen Chen, Ruilong Wu, Yanyan Lan, Ting Ma, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces MolEvolve, an evolutionary framework using LLMs to autonomously evolve libraries of chemical symbolic operations for molecular optimization, addressing activity cliffs and interpretability limitations.

entry.title: Uniform Laws of Large Numbers in Product Spaces

author.name: Ron Holzman, Shay Moran, Alexander Shlimovich

entry.summary: Studies uniform laws of large numbers in cartesian product spaces under absolute continuity with respect to product marginals, showing linear VC dimension characterizes uniform convergence in this setting.

entry.title: How Vulnerable Are Edge LLMs?

author.name: Ao Ding, Hongzong Li, Zi Liang, Zhanpeng Shi, Shuxin Zhuang, Shiqin Tang, Rong Feng, Ping Lu

entry.summary: Studies knowledge extraction attacks on quantized edge-deployed LLMs, showing that quantization doesn't remove semantic knowledge, and proposes CLIQ for structured query construction to improve extraction coverage.

entry.title: COVTrack++: Learning Open-Vocabulary Multi-Object Tracking from Continuous Videos via a Synergistic Paradigm

author.name: Zekun Qian, Wei Feng, Ruize Han, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: COVTrack++ addresses open-vocabulary multi-object tracking by constructing C-TAO (26x annotation density increase) and proposing a synergistic framework for detection and association of arbitrary categories including novel objects.

entry.title: CGRL: Causal-Guided Representation Learning for Graph Out-of-Distribution Generalization

author.name: Bowen Lu, Liangqiang Yang, Teng Li

entry.summary: CGRL uses causal graphs and backdoor adjustment to derive a lower bound for improving GNN out-of-distribution generalization, addressing spurious correlations in node classification.

entry.title: Exploring How Fair Model Representations Relate to Fair Recommendations

author.name: Bj{\o}rnar Vass{\o}y, Benjamin Kille, Helge Langseth

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that removing demographic information from recommender system representations leads to fairer recommendations, comparing representation-level fairness with actual recommendation parity.

entry.title: Fast and Faithful: Real-Time Verification for Long-Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

author.name: Xunzhuo Liu, Bowei He, Xue Liu, Haichen Zhang, Huamin Chen

entry.summary: Presents a real-time verification system for long-document RAG that processes documents up to 32K tokens under latency constraints, enabling full-document grounding in production pipelines.

entry.title: PoliticsBench: Benchmarking Political Values in Large Language Models with Multi-Turn Roleplay

author.name: Rohan Khetan, Ashna Khetan

entry.summary: PoliticsBench evaluates political bias in eight prominent LLMs using a multi-turn roleplay framework adapted from EQ-Bench-v3. Tests whether commercial LLMs display systematic left-leaning bias that becomes more pronounced under roleplay conditions.

entry.title: OmniACBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Context-Grounded Acoustic Control in Omni-Modal Models

author.name: Seunghee Kim, Bumkyu Park, Kyudan Jung, Joosung Lee, Soyoon Kim, Jeonghoon Kim, Taeuk Kim, Hwiyeol Jo

entry.summary: OmniACBench benchmarks context-grounded acoustic control in omni-modal models, evaluating whether models can appropriately modulate speech rate, phonation, emotion, accent, and timbre when reading text aloud given visual context. Tests eight models on 3,559 instances.

entry.title: Thinking with Tables: Enhancing Multi-Modal Tabular Understanding via Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning

author.name: Kun-Yang Yu, Zhi Zhou, Shi-Yu Tian, Xiao-Wen Yang, Zi-Yi Jia, Ming Yang, Zi-Jian Cheng, Lan-Zhe Guo, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: Thinking with Tables (TWT) proposes a neuro-symbolic reasoning mechanism for tabular-vision multi-modal understanding. It uses program-aided code-based reasoning to handle structural variability, complex feature dependencies, and heterogeneous downstream tasks with tables.

entry.title: What and When to Learn: CURriculum Ranking Loss for Large-Scale Speaker Verification

author.name: Massa Baali, Sarthak Bisht, Rita Singh, Bhiksha Raj

entry.summary: Proposes Curry (CURriculum Ranking), an adaptive loss for large-scale speaker verification that estimates sample difficulty online via Sub-center ArcFace. Claims to be the largest-scale speaker verification system trained to date.

entry.title: Prototype Fusion: A Training-Free Multi-Layer Approach to OOD Detection

author.name: Shreen Gul, Mohamed Elmahallawy, Ardhendu Tripathy, Sanjay Madria

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free multi-layer approach to out-of-distribution detection using prototype fusion across multiple network layers.
